title: in vivo Continuous site-specific intravascular monitoring of arterial and venous blood oxygenation.
abstract: Objective Approach. n Main results. Significance. . Conventional pulse oximetry (PO) provides continuous noninvasive arterial oxygen saturation, whereas arterial and venous blood gas analysis provides intermittent reference measurements. Neither modality continuously monitors saturation at a selected deep intravascular site. In this proof-of-concept feasibility study, we assessed whether intravascular diffuse reflectance spectroscopy tracks the direction and time course of prespecified arterial, central venous, and regional renal venous oxygenation changes, alongside conventional PO where an arterial comparator was appropriate.Three separate experimental protocols were performed in three pigs (one animal per protocol;= 1 per condition). Oxygen saturation was monitored with the iBLOS sensing wire in the abdominal aorta during apnea-induced systemic hypoxemia, in the inferior vena cava (IVC) during repeated hypoxic challenges, and in the right renal vein during transient venous outflow obstruction. Conventional PO was recorded concurrently during the arterial and IVC protocols as an arterial monitoring comparator; no blood-gas samples were collected in these feasibility experiments.Continuous intravascular blood oxygenation level monitoring detected rapid and dynamic arterial desaturation and reoxygenation during systemic apnea and demonstrated reproducible responses during repeated hypoxic challenges. Venous oxygenation measured in the IVC exhibited lower baseline oxygen saturation and slower desaturation-recovery kinetics than arterial measurements, reflecting physiological oxygen extraction and circulatory transit delays. During renal vein occlusion, oxygen saturation proximal to the obstruction progressively decreased toward near-complete oxygen depletion before rapidly recovering following restoration of venous outflow. These regional physiological measurements are not feasible using peripheral PO.This feasibility platform provides continuous, site-specific intravascular saturation trends in vascular territories that conventional noninvasive monitoring cannot directly sample. With validation against contemporaneous blood-gas measurements and evaluation in larger studies, it could help fill a monitoring gap during ischemia, reperfusion, and endovascular intervention.

title: Do Preoperative Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists Influence Lumbar Fusion Outcomes? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) are increasingly used in patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes, but lumbar fusion-specific associations with postoperative outcomes remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and surgical and postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing lumbar fusion. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through 14 May 2026. Comparative studies of adults undergoing lumbar fusion with and without preoperative GLP-1RA exposure were included. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies of Interventions (ROBINS-I). Random-effects meta-analyses generated odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. The protocol was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261414637). RESULTS: P P P P Seven retrospective cohorts involving 28,525 patients were included; 6 used propensity score matching or another matching strategy. No statistically significant associations were observed between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and reoperation or revision (OR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.44-1.24;= 0.25), postoperative infection (OR: 0.83, 95% CI: 0.68-1.00;= 0.05), wound complications (OR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.65-1.12;= 0.26), or postoperative respiratory complications (OR: 1.08, 95% CI: 0.63-1.84;= 0.69). Deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and unplanned emergency department visits also did not differ significantly. All included studies were observational and predominantly used large administrative data sources. CONCLUSIONS: Across the evaluated outcomes, the available observational evidence did not identify a signal of increased postoperative risk associated with preoperative GLP-1RA exposure after lumbar fusion. Prospective studies with standardized exposure definitions and perioperative management protocols are warranted to confirm these findings and better define their clinical implications. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current observational evidence does not establish preoperative GLP-1RA exposure alone as an independent risk factor for adverse outcomes after lumbar fusion.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between preoperative GLP-1RA exposure and surgical and postoperative outcomes in adults undergoing lumbar fusion. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception through 14 May 2026.

title: Integration of radiobiological modeling with clinical outcomes for optimizing carotid-sparing treatment planning in head and neck cancers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) can deliver significant incidental doses to the carotid arteries, increasing the risk of late vascular events. Carotid-sparing intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) with radiobiological modelling may reduce these risks without compromising tumour control. OBJECTIVE: To assess the predictive accuracy of normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) modelling for carotid stenosis and its association with tumour control, vascular events, and quality of life in HNSCC patients treated with carotid-sparing IMRT. METHODS: In this prospective observational study, 120 patients with HNSCC underwent carotid-sparing IMRT. Dose-volume histograms were used to calculate NTCP for carotid stenosis using the Lyman-Kutcher-Burman model, and tumour control probability (TCP) from target coverage. Patients were followed for ≥5 years with Doppler ultrasonography, MRI angiography when indicated, neurocognitive testing, and EORTC QLQ-H and N35 questionnaires. The primary endpoint was correlation between NTCP and ≥50% radiographically confirmed carotid stenosis. Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression, and ROC analyses were performed. RESULTS: At 5 years, high NTCP (>8%) was associated with reduced stenosis-free survival compared to low NTCP (≤5%) (HR = 5.62; 95% CI: 2.1-14.8; P < 0.001). NTCP correlated with incidence of ≥50% stenosis ( r = 0.78; P < 0.001) and cerebrovascular events ( P = 0.002). ROC analysis demonstrated good predictive accuracy (AUC = 0.84). TCP remained >90% across all NTCP quartiles. Low NTCP was associated with slower intima-media thickness progression and better neurocognitive and quality-of-life scores. CONCLUSION: NTCP modelling reliably predicts late carotid stenosis and vascular outcomes in HNSCC patients receiving IMRT and supports patient-specific carotid-sparing strategies.

title: Maternal Mortality Across a Multi-Hospital Health System in Saudi Arabia: A Retrospective Study (2016-2024).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Maternal mortality remains a pressing global health challenge and is a vital indicator of healthcare quality. Despite improvements in Saudi Arabia, preventable maternal fatalities continue to occur, with insufficient research on regional disparities. OBJECTIVE: This study seeks to assess the maternal mortality ratio (MMR) and its causes across five hospitals within the Ministry of National Guard Health Affairs in Saudi Arabia and evaluate it is main causes,thereby addressing a gap in maternal mortality data in the Gulf region. METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, descriptive study included all maternal deaths occurring during pregnancy or within 42 days postpartum between 2016 and 2024 across five National Guard hospitals in Riyadh, Jeddah, Madinah, Al-Ahsa, and Dammam. Data were extracted from hospital records and analyzed descriptively using SPSS version 28. RESULTS: Eighteen maternal deaths were identified over the nine-year period, yielding an overall MMR of 6.2 per 100,000 live births (mean age at death 29.8 ± 6.3 years). MMR varied considerably by year, from 0.00/100,000 in 2017 to 37.5/100,000 in 2020. Pregnancy-related complications accounted for 50% of deaths (9/18), most commonly venous thromboembolism (66.7%). Non-obstetric causes included COVID-19 (16.7%), unknown cause (16.7%), brain tumor (5.6%), and myocarditis (5.6%). Most deaths occurred in women with parity 1-3 (61.1%), split evenly between vaginal and caesarean delivery (50% each). Geographic variation was marked: Riyadh recorded deaths in most years with a peak in 2020; Dammam and Al-Ahsa each showed sporadic extreme spikes; Jeddah showed intermittent elevations; no deaths occurred in Madinah. CONCLUSION: The overall MMR at these hospitals is comparatively low to global figures, significant variations across different cities and years, alongside a notable number of deaths with unspecified causes, underscore the need for standardized mortality reviews, autopsy confirmations for suspected embolic deaths, and continuous targeted monitoring.

title: Comparison of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters versus Central Venous Catheters in a Medical Intensive Care Unit: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients in medical intensive care units (MICUs) often require prolonged intravenous therapy, making optimal catheter selection critical. While central venous catheters (CVCs) remain common, peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are increasingly used. This single-centre retrospective study compared indwelling time, clinical utility, and complication profiles between PICCs and CVCs in MICU patients. METHODS: We analyzed 276 MICU patients with either a PICC or CVC, comparing catheter selection, length of stay, dwell time, and complication rates. Complication rates were also standardized per 1000 catheter-days. RESULTS: P P P P P P P P P P P P PICCs were used more frequently in patients with malignancy (< 0.001) or requiring chemotherapy (< 0.001), whereas CVCs were preferred in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (= 0.012), diabetes (= 0.012), COVID-19 (= 0.020), or vasopressor infusion (= 0.001). PICCs were associated with longer indwelling times (≥12 days,< 0.001). In the unstandardized analysis, PICCs had higher rates of catheter dislodgement (< 0.001) and occlusion (= 0.005), but lower rates of puncture-site complications (bleeding, hypersensitivity, fluid leakage; all< 0.05) and deep vein thrombosis incidence (= 0.038). After standardization per 1,000 catheter-days, dislodgement remained significantly more frequent with PICCs, whereas the difference in occlusion was no longer statistically significant. No bloodstream infections occurred with PICCs, versus 5.4% with CVCs (= 0.169). Because groups differed substantially in patient selection, clinical indication, dwell time, insertion site, and securement method, these findings should be interpreted as associations rather than evidence of superiority. CONCLUSION: PICCs were associated with longer indwelling times and a higher rate of dislodgement, but lower rates of puncture-site complications and deep vein thrombosis; the difference in occlusion was no longer significant after standardization. Vascular access selection should be individualized according to patient characteristics, therapy requirements, anticipated duration, and device-related risks.

While central venous catheters (CVCs) remain common, peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are increasingly used. This single-centre retrospective study compared indwelling time, clinical utility, and complication profiles between PICCs and CVCs in MICU patients.

title: Age-adjusted and probability-adjusted D-dimer thresholds for the diagnosis of acute DVT: a narrative review.
abstract: In patients presenting to emergency departments with symptoms of lower-limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT), systematically ordering a compression ultrasonography (CUS) in all to rule out DVT contributes to crowding and low-yield testing. Contemporary diagnostic strategies aim at improving efficiency by avoiding the need for a CUS, while maintaining safety, as assessed by low short-term venous thromboembolism (VTE) rates among patients with a negative diagnostic work-up. This narrative review summarizes recent evidence, mainly from prospective management studies, supporting refined D-dimer-based pathways for first-episode DVT, and emerging data in patients with suspected recurrent DVT. In ADJUST-DVT, an age-adjusted D-dimer threshold (age×10 μg/L for ≥50 years) applied to outpatients with a non-high/unlikely pretest probability increased the proportion of patients ruled out without ultrasound by 7% overall as compared with the conventional 500 μg/L cutoff, with the largest gains in those ≥75 years. No failures were identified in patients with a D-dimer level 500 μg/L or greater but below the age-adjusted cutoff (0%, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0%-2.3%). In the 4D study, a clinical probability-adjusted D-dimer strategy (low Wells with D-dimer <1000 μg/L; moderate Wells with <500 μg/L) achieved a 0.6% 3-month VTE rate while reducing ultrasound use by 47%. In patients with a suspected recurrent ipsilateral DVT, D-dimer levels are often higher than in patients without previous DVT and are therefore less useful to exclude the disease. In this situation, a negative D-dimer test may also be associated with a higher failure rate. Indeed, in the PREDICTORS study, a higher-than-expected prevalence of recurrent VTE at presentation in patients with a non-high pretest probability and a negative D-dimer was reported. While CUS is also frequently non-diagnostic due to residual thrombi, the THEIA Study showed that magnetic resonance direct thrombus imaging (MRDTI) can safely guide management as a single test. Together, these studies support practical, outcome-validated approaches that improve diagnostic efficiency and may facilitate implementation in real-world workflows, while highlighting the need for accurate pretest assessment and continued prospective validation of simplified algorithms.

This narrative review summarizes recent evidence, mainly from prospective management studies, supporting refined D-dimer-based pathways for first-episode DVT, and emerging data in patients with suspected recurrent DVT.

title: Endovascular management of acute and chronic arterial mesenteric ischaemia: A narrative review of evidence informing interventional radiology treatment.
abstract: Mesenteric ischaemia is a potentially life-threatening vascular disorder caused by impaired intestinal perfusion, with treatment selection requiring consideration of clinical presentation, bowel viability and lesion anatomy. This narrative review examines evidence informing interventional radiology decisions in arterial acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) and chronic mesenteric ischaemia (CMI). MEDLINE/PubMed was searched from inception to December 31, 2025, supplemented by reference-list screening and targeted guideline searches. Qualitative evidence synthesis considered patient selection, study design, adjunctive treatments, outcomes and follow-up. In AMI, endovascular techniques can restore perfusion, but predominantly retrospective evidence does not establish superiority over surgery in bowel preservation or survival. For CMI requiring revascularisation, European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommend an initial endovascular approach, supported by Cardiovascular and Interventional Radiological Society of Europe consensus-based guidance. Observational comparisons associate endovascular treatment with lower perioperative morbidity, and surgery with less symptom recurrence. By linking individual treatment decisions to society guidance and supporting studies, this review complements existing comprehensive reviews and guidance documents. It distinguishes formal recommendations and consensus-based practice from technical feasibility and demonstrated comparative patient benefit, while identifying unresolved questions concerning AMI reperfusion strategies and device selection, in addition to antithrombotic therapy and restenosis management in CMI.

title: Inflammation and thrombosis: from pathophysiology to future treatments.
abstract: Inflammation and coagulation are tightly interconnected host-defense systems that, when dysregulated, promote pathological thrombosis. This narrative review examines mechanisms, clinical settings, and therapeutic implications of thromboinflammation (TI) across venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, with particular attention to the differences in clinical translation among vascular territories. Endothelial activation, tissue factor expression, platelet-leukocyte interactions, neutrophil extracellular traps, complement activation, inflammasome signalling, and impaired fibrinolysis converge to generate a procoagulant phenotype. These mechanisms modify Virchow's triad and contribute to venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, although their relative importance varies across vascular territories. Clinically, TI is relevant in inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatologic and other immune-mediated disorders, sepsis, coronavirus disease 2019, clonal haematopoiesis, complement-mediated diseases, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. TI offers a unifying framework for mechanistic risk assessment and therapeutic development. In atherothrombosis, randomised trials have demonstrated that selective modulation of inflammatory pathways, particularly the NLRP3-interleukin-1β-interleukin-6 axis and colchicine-sensitive pathways, can reduce recurrent cardiovascular events. By contrast, the role of inflammation-targeted therapies for primary or secondary prevention of VTE remains uncertain. Future studies should identify disease-specific biomarkers and test targeted anti-inflammatory or immunothrombotic strategies, alone or alongside anticoagulation, to prevent thrombosis without compromising haemostasis effectively.

title: Pseudodominant inheritance in paraplegin (SPG7)-associated CPEO-ataxia syndrome.
abstract: SPG7 encodes paraplegin, a mitochondrial AAA-metalloprotease critical for inner mitochondrial membrane protein quality control. Pathogenic variants most commonly cause autosomal recessive hereditary spastic paraplegia (HSP) but its phenotypic spectrum includes cerebellar ataxia, progressive external ophthalmoplegia, myopathy and parkinsonism.We report a 47 year old man presenting with a progressive external ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, progressive gait disturbance, and spasticity. Ten-year follow-up of this individual showed slowly progressive spastic ataxia with ocular motor involvement and neurogenic bladder. His mother and maternal aunt both had marked spasticity, ataxia, ptosis and external ophthalmoplegia. Genetic testing demonstrated compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in paraplegin in this individual. Genetic testing in his mother and aunt revealed homozygous canonical splice-site variants (c.2182-2 A > G). Cascade testing of his asymptomatic father showed a common pathogenic missense variant p.(Ala510Val) in the same gene.This family demonstrates a pseudodominant inheritance pattern, instead of the expected autosomal recessive trait that applies to paraplegin. We highlight diagnostic pitfalls in relying on family history and assumed inheritance traits. We emphasise the importance of segregation analysis and comprehensive genomic testing. Recognition of pseudodominance inheritance has important implications for genetic counselling, family planning and cascade testing.

title: Hemorrhagic Vocal Fold Inflammation Following Endotracheal Intubation in a Patient Undergoing Endovascular Neurosurgery Under Dual Antiplatelet Therapy: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hemorrhagic vocal fold inflammation is an uncommon complication of endotracheal intubation. Its clinical course in patients receiving perioperative antithrombotic therapy remains unclear. CASE PRESENTATION: A woman in her 60 s receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) underwent endovascular neurosurgery with flow-diverter stent deployment and coil embolization. Endotracheal intubation was uneventful, and cuff pressure was appropriately maintained. Hoarseness developed on postoperative day 1, and laryngoscopy on day 2 revealed hemorrhagic vocal fold inflammation. Intraoperative fluoroscopic images suggested proximal migration of the endotracheal tube, with possible changes in tube and cuff position that may have contributed to minor vocal fold mucosal injury. The symptoms improved with conservative management, and complete recovery was confirmed at 1 month. DISCUSSION: Hemorrhagic vocal fold inflammation occurred following apparently uneventful endotracheal intubation in a patient receiving perioperative antithrombotic therapy. Although the underlying mechanism remains uncertain, changes in endotracheal tube and cuff position during the procedure represent one possible contributing factor.

Its clinical course in patients receiving perioperative antithrombotic therapy remains unclear. CASE PRESENTATION: A woman in her 60 s receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) underwent endovascular neurosurgery with flow-diverter stent deployment and coil embolization.

title: Maternal Obesity Is Associated With Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Matched Electronic Health Record Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We sought to define the prevalence of obesity in the first trimester of pregnancy among women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and evaluate its association with adverse pregnancy outcomes. METHODS: First-trimester body mass index (BMI) was assessed in pregnancies with and without IBD. Pregnancies reaching 24 weeks were propensity-score matched 1:6 by maternal age, BMI, smoking status and gravidity to assess whether IBD conferred additional pregnancy risk. RESULTS: Overall, 22.6% (64/283; 95% CI 17.7%-27.5%) of pregnancies in women with IBD met ethnicity-adjusted criteria for obesity. Increasing obesity class was associated with stepwise increases in gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, venous thromboembolism (VTE), emergency caesarean section and high birthweight. Matching yielded 177 IBD pregnancies and 1062 controls. Obesity was independently associated with the composite adverse pregnancy outcome (OR 1.63; 95% CI 1.15-2.33; p = 0.007), whereas no statistically significant additional association was identified for IBD diagnosis alone (OR 0.74; 95% CI 0.53-1.03; p = 0.073). Among IBD pregnancies, aspirin was recommended in 39.3% (86/219). Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) was prescribed in 21.6% (19/88) of pregnancies classified post hoc as intermediate or high VTE risk. CONCLUSION: More than one in five pregnancies in women with IBD were complicated by obesity. Obesity was strongly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, whereas this study did not identify a significant additional effect attributable to IBD diagnosis alone. Preventive prescribing with aspirin and LMWH represents an opportunity for improved antenatal care.

METHODS: First-trimester body mass index (BMI) was assessed in pregnancies with and without IBD. Pregnancies reaching 24 weeks were propensity-score matched 1:6 by maternal age, BMI, smoking status and gravidity to assess whether IBD conferred additional pregnancy risk.

title: Doppler Ultrasonography and Computed Tomography Angiography in Carotid Artery Stenosis: Discordance and Its Potential Impact on Surgical Decision-Making.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The degree of carotid artery stenosis influences surgical decision-making; therefore, accurate assessment is essential for appropriate patient selection. This study evaluated agreement between Doppler ultrasonography (DUS) and computed tomography angiography (CTA) in patients with significant stenosis detected on DUS and investigated factors associated with discordance. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 79 patients who underwent DUS between January 2024 and October 2025 were included. DUS stenosis grade, CTA stenosis according to NASCET and ECST methods, lumen diameters, plaque characteristics, and accompanying vascular features were evaluated. RESULTS: Agreement between DUS and CTA was fair using NASCET (κ = 0.413; p < .001) and moderate using ECST (κ = 0.531; p < .001). Agreement between NASCET and ECST was substantial (κ = 0.799; p < .001). Discordance was most frequent in the 50-69% DUS stenosis group and varied according to stenosis severity and CTA measurement method. Plaque type, plaque length, and calcification were not associated with discordance. Residual lumen diameter on CTA was significantly larger in NASCET-based discordant cases (p = .018) whereas no significant difference was observed using ECST classification. In some patients, discrepancies could potentially affect surgical decision-making. CONCLUSION: Agreement between DUS and CTA in significant carotid stenosis was fair using NASCET and moderate using ECST, with discordance particularly frequent in the 50-69% stenosis group and dependent on the CTA measurement method. Combined assessment with 2 noninvasive imaging modalities may help reduce misclassification in patients considered for surgical treatment.

This study evaluated agreement between Doppler ultrasonography (DUS) and computed tomography angiography (CTA) in patients with significant stenosis detected on DUS and investigated factors associated with discordance. METHODS: In this retrospective study, 79 patients who underwent DUS between January 2024 and October 2025 were included.

title: Development of a machine learning model to predict venous thromboembolism risk in women using combined oral contraceptives.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with combined oral contraceptives (COCPs) being a modifiable risk factor. Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users. METHODS: This study was conducted using data from the Saudi Real-World Evidence Network (2016–2023). The primary outcome was the first VTE event within 2 years of COCP initiation. Following data partitioning, feature selection was performed on the training set. Elastic-net logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), one-class support vector machine and Isolation-Forest were trained on original and resampled datasets. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and F1 score. RESULTS: The cohort included 24 518 treatment episodes (n=17 512, VTE events=52). After handling class imbalance, RF and XGBoost were the best-performing models (F1: 84.3% and 81.6%; AUROC: 59.6% and 69.2%, respectively), compared with other models (F1: 2.6%–55.3%, AUROC: 54.2%–68.4%). Key predictors included age, glucocorticoid use and rheumatic, renal and thyroid diseases. DISCUSSION: ML shows potential for VTE risk detection despite low event rate and class imbalance. However, findings suggest synthetic sample overfitting, and external validation is warranted before clinical deployment. Identified predictors reinforce the role of metabolic and inflammatory factors in VTE susceptibility among COCP users. CONCLUSION: ML models, particularly XGBoost and RF, demonstrated moderate predictive ability for VTE among COCP users, supporting their use in individualised risk assessments, though external validation is warranted.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with combined oral contraceptives (COCPs) being a modifiable risk factor. Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users.

title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults With Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: A NHANES Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 participants aged >=40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI <=0.90. A NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up ten steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment. RESULTS: The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (OR 1.748, 95% CI 1.218-2.510; P=0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (HR 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P=0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P=0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P=0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability. CONCLUSIONS: Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2004 participants aged >=40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI <=0.90.

title: Common Femoral Atherectomy yields safe results and low morbidity in the outpatient setting.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy is considered the gold standard for the treatment of CFA disease. Some patients with CFA occlusive disease have significant comorbidities that may prevent them from undergoing open surgery. Several endovascular treatment options for the CFA, such as atherectomy, angioplasty, and stenting, are available but have not been widely adopted. This study aimed to describe our experience expanding the use of atherectomy in the outpatient setting for the treatment of CFA disease. METHODS: This is a single-institution, retrospective review of 49 CFA atherectomy procedures performed from January 2017 to November 2022 at Trinity Health Ann Arbor. Primary outcomes included primary patency at 1 year and MALE-free survival. Secondary outcomes involved changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI), toe pressures, and morbidity at 90 days. RESULTS: 49 CFA atherectomies were performed on 45 patients (73 yo ± 7 years), 45% with claudication and 55% with critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). TASC classification of the treated lesions was TASC A in 4%, TASC B in 29%, TASC C in 61%, and TASC D in 6%. Three patients also underwent superficial femoral artery (SFA) stenting; one had concomitant CFA stenting, and 24 (49%) underwent treatment distal to the CFA atherectomy site. We encountered three complications: one readmission for dehydration, one postoperative hematoma, and one focal SFA dissection requiring delayed secondary stent placement. There were no deaths within 90 days. Post-procedure, the average ABI increased from 0.59 to 0.80 (P<0.01), and toe pressure rose from 42 to 68 (P<0.01). Thirty-five cases had follow-up of at least one year, showing a primary patency rate of 86% and a 94% MALE-free at one year. Additionally, 71% reported symptom improvement or wound healing at their last follow-up. CONCLUSION: When open surgery may be medically prohibited, CFA atherectomy combined with balloon angioplasty can be performed safely, yielding good clinical outcomes as a standalone procedure or with additional infrainguinal interventions. When applied in appropriate clinical and radiologic circumstances, patients experience favorable outcomes with low procedural morbidity. Due to its clinical benefits and low risk, this procedure can be a valuable addition to the modern vascular surgeon's treatment armamentarium.

Some patients with CFA occlusive disease have significant comorbidities that may prevent them from undergoing open surgery. Several endovascular treatment options for the CFA, such as atherectomy, angioplasty, and stenting, are available but have not been widely adopted.

title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality. RESULTS: The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs 6.6% vs 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend= 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively). CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short- and long-term outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

title: Guideline-to-Practice Gap in Ankle-Brachial Index Screening Among Inpatients with Newly Documented Lower Extremity Wounds.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common and underdiagnosed. Hospitalized patients with lower extremity wounds may represent a missed opportunity for recognition. This study described inpatient ankle-brachial index (ABI) screening patterns in this population. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to two hospitals within a single urban academic health system in 2025 with a new lower extremity wound documented in nursing wound flowsheets. Recent screening was defined as ABI testing performed during the index hospitalization or within one year prior to admission. Patient and admission characteristics were compared by screening status, and logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with screening. Wound location and noninvasive vascular testing results were summarized descriptively. RESULTS: Among 2244 inpatients with newly documented lower extremity wounds, 343 patients (15.3%) were screened with ABIs. Screened patients were younger (65 vs 69 years; P<.001) and had a higher burden of atherosclerotic or diabetic comorbidities. After multivariable adjustment, pre-existing PAD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.79; P<.001), diabetes mellitus (aOR, 2.72; P<.001), and end-stage renal disease (aOR, 1.60; P=.021) were independently associated with ABI screening. Female sex was associated with lower odds of screening (aOR, 0.73; P=.045). Compared with medicine or hospitalist services, admission to general surgery/acute care surgery (aOR, 2.15; P=.002) and vascular surgery (aOR, 4.29; P<.001) was associated with higher odds of screening. Screening proportions were 23.6% for toe wounds, 20.6% for ankle/Achilles wounds, 19.9% for foot/heel wounds, and 12.8% for lower leg wounds. Among screened patients with available measurements, 50.4% had an abnormal ABI, 63.8% had an abnormal TBI, and 69.0% had at least one abnormal ABI or TBI. CONCLUSION: PAD screening was performed in a minority of hospitalized patients with newly documented lower extremity wounds and was associated with recognized vascular risk factors and admitting service. Abnormal physiologic testing was common among screened patients. Standardized wound-triggered screening pathways may reduce missed opportunities for vascular evaluation.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common and underdiagnosed. Hospitalized patients with lower extremity wounds may represent a missed opportunity for recognition. This study described inpatient ankle-brachial index (ABI) screening patterns in this population.

title: Long-term Outcomes of Primary Femoropopliteal Stents: A Retrospective Multi-Centre Experience and the Role for a Doppler Ultrasound Surveillance Programme.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularisation is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating re-intervention, remains a challenge. This study performs a retrospective outcomes analysis to suggest which patient populations may benefit from a Doppler ultrasound (DUS) surveillance programme in improving primary patency and amputation-free survival following femoropopliteal stenting in patients with PAD. METHODS: A multicentre, retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from patients who underwent femoropopliteal stenting between January 2015 and April 2023 within a vascular network with six hospital sites. Data were collected from 238 stents in 220 patients. Demographics, stent characteristics, and surveillance protocols were analysed. Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models were used to identify risk factors for primary patency and amputation-free survival. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were generated for both outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to compare outcomes between supra-popliteal and infra-popliteal stents. RESULTS: A total of 238 stents were inserted in a population comprised of 28.6% females, with the median age of 72.5 +/- 11.5 years. In 74.8% (178) of cases, patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Primary patency rates at 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years were 90%, 67.7%, 51.2%, 26.6%, and 11.7%, respectively. The average amputation-free survival was 3.2 years. Cox regression identified CLTI (hazard ratio, 6.37, p = .001), type 1 diabetes mellitus (hazard ratio, 3.16, p = .006), and female sex (hazard ratio, 1.69, P = .037) as significant predictors of loss of primary patency. Drug-eluting stents and diabetes were associated with poorer amputation-free survival. CONCLUSIONS: The study illustrates a cohort of high-risk patients, particularly those with CLTI and diabetes, who may benefit from future enrolment in an enhanced DUS surveillance programme targeted to improve long-term outcomes. However, further research is required to explore the clinical-effectiveness, cost-effectiveness and implementation feasibility of such programmes in clinical practice.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularisation is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating re-intervention, remains a challenge.

title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetes-Related Foot Disease: An Arterial-Wall Dimension Uncharacterized in Current Limb Staging.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To synthesize the evidence on medial arterial calcification (MAC) in diabetes-related foot disease, addressing its arterial-wall phenotype, effects on haemodynamic assessment, prognostic associations, and its potential role in limb staging. METHODS: Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischaemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS). RESULTS: MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis. An elevated ankle-brachial index is uninterpretable, and a reference-range value does not exclude peripheral artery disease. Across cohorts of differing design and definition, MAC has been consistently associated with major amputation, delayed wound healing and mortality, in line with a systematic review of 51 calcification-scoring studies; the five-point pedal score has been externally validated, and associations persisted after adjustment for WIfI stage. Model comparison in one cohort suggests incremental information, but discrimination, calibration and reclassification beyond established staging have not been reported. Neither WIfI nor GLASS characterizes arterial-wall phenotype. CONCLUSIONS: The consistency and reproducibility of the prognostic evidence justify formal consideration of MAC in forthcoming revisions of limb-staging systems and guidelines. Incremental-value analyses should accompany that evaluation and inform the form of any modifier rather than delay it. One concrete route is to use MAC as a qualifier of the reliability of the WIfI ischaemia grade in the individual limb.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: To synthesize the evidence on medial arterial calcification (MAC) in diabetes-related foot disease, addressing its arterial-wall phenotype, effects on haemodynamic assessment, prognostic associations, and its potential role in limb staging. METHODS: Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischaemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS). RESULTS: MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis.

title: Five-Year Outcomes of Covered Stent-Graft Repair for Traumatic and Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Injuries.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular repair with covered stent-grafts offers a prompt and effective strategy to manage lower-extremity arterial trauma and catheterization-related iatrogenic vascular complications. However, long-term durability and late complication profiles of covered stent-grafts in the femoral segments remain poorly defined. The aim of the study was to evaluate the long-term outcomes of covered stent-grafting for traumatic and iatrogenic injuries of the common, superficial, and deep femoral arteries over a 5-year follow-up period. METHODS: In this single-center retrospective study, 58 consecutive patients (40 males [69.0%]; mean age: 57 ± 13.6 years) who underwent endovascular repair for femoral arterial injuries between August 2011 and August 2021 were analyzed. The primary outcome was the 5-year primary patency rate. Secondary outcomes included primary-assisted and secondary patency rates, as well as subgroup comparisons of patency based on stent-graft type, lesion type, and injury type. RESULTS: Etiologies included iatrogenic injury in 36 patients (62.1%) and traumatic injury in 22 patients (37.9%). Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases. The overall 5-year Kaplan-Meier estimates for primary, primary-assisted, and secondary patency rates were 72.4%, 91.4%, and 94.8%, respectively, with a mean primary patency duration of 52 months. Log-rank tests demonstrated no statistically significant differences in primary patency rates across stent-graft types (p = 0.942), lesion types (p = 0.751), or injury types (p = 0.864). CONCLUSION: In appropriately selected patients, covered stent-graft repair was associated with high technical success, low observed complication rates, and favorable long-term patency for traumatic and iatrogenic femoral arterial injuries.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Endovascular repair with covered stent-grafts offers a prompt and effective strategy to manage lower-extremity arterial trauma and catheterization-related iatrogenic vascular complications. However, long-term durability and late complication profiles of covered stent-grafts in the femoral segments remain poorly defined. The aim of the study was to evaluate the long-term outcomes of covered stent-grafting for traumatic and iatrogenic injuries of the common, superficial, and deep femoral arteries over a 5-year follow-up period.

title: Brachial Plexus Injuries from Overhead Arm Positioning During F/BEVAR: A Case Series and Call for Standardized Technique.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Overhead arm positioning during fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) may improve imaging quality and reduce procedural radiation dose. Elevated arm positioning during general anesthesia, however, may result in risk for nerve symptoms. The aim of this study was to assess the occurrence of upper extremity symptoms (UES) after overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR. DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, cohort. METHODS: All consecutive patients undergoing F/BEVAR performed with bilateral overhead arm positioning at *our* Hospital between 2023 and 2025 were included. Neutral head position, padded overhead support, and abduction limited to ≤90° were used in accordance with standardized positioning protocols. Demographic, comorbidity, and procedural data were accessed from the clinical records. The primary aim was to evaluate the rate of post-operative UES and brachial plexus injury (BPI). In cases with BPI, neurological consultation and rehabilitation outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: Among 67 patients who underwent F/BEVAR with bilateral overhead arm position, six patients (9.0%) developed postoperative UES. Two patients (3.0%) had neurologist-confirmed BPI; one developed bilateral palsy with partial recovery after 8 weeks, while the other developed unilateral palsy with complete recovery by 3 months. Neither patient required surgical intervention, The remaining four patients (6.0%) experienced minor transient UES. There was no difference in baseline parameters between patients with and without UES. Urgent repair was more frequent among patients experiencing any UES than among those without UES (50.0% vs 9.8%; p = 0.028). Both patients with BPI underwent procedures lasting >180 minutes. Procedural technical success was 98.5%, and in-hospital mortality 1.5%. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR was associated with a measurable incidence of UES. Although most symptoms were transient and resolved without intervention, clinically significant BPI occurred in a small proportion of patients despite standardized positioning. These findings support cautious and selective use of prolonged overhead arm positioning and warrant prospective evaluation of safe positioning duration and patient-related susceptibility.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Overhead arm positioning during fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) may improve imaging quality and reduce procedural radiation dose. Elevated arm positioning during general anesthesia, however, may result in risk for nerve symptoms. The aim of this study was to assess the occurrence of upper extremity symptoms (UES) after overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR.

title: From Virtual Reality to High-Fidelity Silicone Models: A Pilot Pathway for Training Vascular Surgeons in Robotic Skills.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This pilot study evaluated the learning curve of vascular surgeons undergoing structured VR simulator training and assessed the feasibility of performing a robotic vascular anastomosis within a team lacking prior laparoscopic or robotic experience. METHODS: Three vascular surgeons completed a structured curriculum on the RobotiX Mentor VR simulator, followed by a robotic aorto-aortic bypass with a Dacron graft performed on a high-fidelity pulsatile silicone model using the da Vinci surgical system. These procedures were compared with an open-technique anastomosis performed on the same model, with outcomes assessed via the Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills (OSATS), operative time, and leakage rate. RESULTS: Surgeons completed a median of 248 training sessions across 77 distinct cases to reach the 20-hour required for robotic surgery certification, with proficiency achieved after 14-19 hours of training. Robotic anastomosis was associated with lower OSATS scores (34.5 [IQR 33.25-35.375] vs 40 [IQR 40-40]; P=0.003) and longer operative times (47 [IQR 41.5-57.75] vs 12 minutes [IQR 11.0-13.75]) relative to open surgery. Leakage rates did not differ between techniques (2 mL [IQR 0-4] vs 0 mL; P=0.087), and final product quality was considered acceptable, with a median score of 23 out of 25. CONCLUSION: Vascular surgeons without prior robotic or laparoscopic experience were able to acquire basic robotic vascular anastomosis skills through a structured curriculum combining VR and high-fidelity silicone simulation. Despite longer operative times relative to open surgery, technical quality and leakage rates were comparable between techniques.

title: Generalist vascular training in a subspecialising specialty: operative exposure and workforce implications from a national UK vascular surgery eLogbook analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Vascular surgery became a standalone specialty in the United Kingdom (UK) in 2012, breaking away from general surgery, with trainees completing a 6-year Higher Specialty Training (HST) programme to attain a Certificate of Completion of Training (CCT) in vascular surgery. Operative exposure in this new training programme and time to CCT remain poorly described, with implications for workforce planning and training structure. METHODS: A retrospective observational analysis of anonymised eLogbook data was performed for all National Training Number holders awarded CCT in vascular surgery between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2024. Data were obtained from the Joint Committee on Surgical Training and mapped to ten portfolio index procedural categories. RESULTS: Thirty-six trainees achieved CCT during the study period. Fewer than half completed within the planned 6-year duration (median 6.75 years, IQR 6-8.63). In total, 48 636 operative cases were logged, and median active operative participation was 1 000 cases per trainee(IQR 901 - 1 161). Major and minor amputations, alongside debridement formed the largest index category (192 cases, IQR 138 - 232); vascular access surgery was the lowest (38 cases, IQR 21 - 72). When AAA repair was considered as two distinct procedures, median exposure for both open and endovascular repair fell below that of vascular access surgery. CONCLUSIONS: Training duration routinely exceeds the nominal 6-year pathway, with implications for workforce supply modelling. Operative exposure is unevenly distributed, raising questions about the adequacy of a generalist training model in a subspecialising specialty and the role of targeted post-CCT fellowship provision.

Operative exposure in this new training programme and time to CCT remain poorly described, with implications for workforce planning and training structure. METHODS: A retrospective observational analysis of anonymised eLogbook data was performed for all National Training Number holders awarded CCT in vascular surgery between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2024.

title: Comparative Perioperative Outcomes of Rescue FEVAR vs Open Repair for Failed EVAR.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Redo aortic repair following previous endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is often technically challenging and associated with significant morbidity. Technologic advances in custom modified grafts have permitted increased utilization of endovascular versus open repairs. Despite this progress, there is limited data surrounding the comparative perioperative outcomes between these procedural approaches. METHODS: The National Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients undergoing elective open abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair or fenestrated endovascular aortic repair (FEVAR) with a physician-modified (PMEG) or custom graft (CMD) following a previous EVAR from 2010 to 2024. A univariate analysis to compare groups was completed with chi square and Fisher's Exact T-test, and outcomes were compared using multivariate logistic and linear regression. Data was analyzed using STATA. RESULTS: 900 patients underwent open repair, and 651 patents underwent FEVAR following previous EVAR. Using multivariate linear regression, patients undergoing open repair had an increased risk of postoperative pneumonia (OR 6.23, p=0.001), postoperative reintubation (OR 2.01, p=0.005), and major adverse cardiac events (OR 2.16, p=0.001) compared to patients undergoing FEVAR. Patients undergoing open repair had a higher risk of mortality (OR 2.02, p=0.018) and were less likely to be discharged home (OR 0.47, p<0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Complex endovascular rescue of previously failed EVAR is associated with decreased the rate of perioperative complications compared to an open approach. FEVAR utilizing PMEG or CMD may be considered as a viable option in patients who are undergoing elective redo AAA repair following a failed EVAR.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Redo aortic repair following previous endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is often technically challenging and associated with significant morbidity. Technologic advances in custom modified grafts have permitted increased utilization of endovascular versus open repairs. Despite this progress, there is limited data surrounding the comparative perioperative outcomes between these procedural approaches.

title: Long-Term Patency and Clinical Outcomes After Retrograde Mesenteric Bypass for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is an uncommon yet clinically significant condition resulting from insufficient blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract, frequently leading to severe symptoms and increased morbidity. Although endovascular therapy has become the initial treatment strategy in many centres, open surgical reconstruction remains an important option for selected patients. This study evaluated long-term graft patency and clinical outcomes after retrograde mesenteric bypass. METHODS: We evaluated 34 patients treated with retrograde mesenteric bypass for CMI between 2009 and 2024. Patency rates were measured with Kaplan-Meier analysis. Thrombosis was classified as early (≤30 days), mid-term (31-365 days), or late (>365 days). RESULTS: Superior mesenteric artery bypass was performed in 33 patients (97.1%), celiac bypass in 25 (73.5%), and dual-vessel reconstruction in 24 (70.6%). Median follow-up was 2737 days (IQR, 1760-4353), approximately 7.5 years. No early thrombosis occurred. Two mid-term and three late occlusions were observed. Primary patency rates were 93.3% at 1 and 3 years, 89.4% at 5 years, and 85.0% at 10 years. Clinical symptoms resolved after revascularisation in all patients surviving the perioperative period, and no recurrent symptoms were documented during follow-up. No patient required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Retrograde mesenteric bypass was associated with stable long-term patency, sustained symptom resolution, and low perioperative mortality. It remains a durable open surgical option for chronic mesenteric ischemia, particularly when endovascular revascularisation is not feasible or is unlikely to provide durable results.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) is an uncommon yet clinically significant condition resulting from insufficient blood flow to the gastrointestinal tract, frequently leading to severe symptoms and increased morbidity. Although endovascular therapy has become the initial treatment strategy in many centres, open surgical reconstruction remains an important option for selected patients. This study evaluated long-term graft patency and clinical outcomes after retrograde mesenteric bypass.

title: A Scoping Review on Artificial Intelligence for Image-Based Analysis in Aortic Aneurysm Care.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach to enhance automated image analysis, quantitative assessment, and clinical decision-making in aortic aneurysm care. This scoping review aims to summarize the current cumulative body of evidence. METHODS: A systematic PubMed search identified 661 records, with 59 studies ultimately included after de-duplication and multi-stage screening based on predefined eligibility criteria, focusing on original research applying artificial intelligence to medical imaging in aortic aneurysm care. Data were extracted on study design, imaging modality, AI methodology, validation, and dataset characteristics. RESULTS: Fifty-nine studies were included. Deep learning approaches, particularly U-Net-based architectures, were the most frequently applied methods, with AI primarily used for automated segmentation and quantitative analysis of aortic pathology. AI models achieved high technical performance across applications, including vessel segmentation, aneurysm detection, endoleak identification, and risk prediction, with reported improvements in efficiency and diagnostic accuracy. However, external validation, multimodal data integration, and prospective clinical evaluation remained uncommon. CONCLUSION: AI demonstrates substantial potential to enhance aortic aneurysm disease assessment through accurate image analysis, automated quantification, and improved procedural support. However, current limitations include lack of external validation, reporting transparency, and clinical integration.

title: Impact of Angiographic Lesion Distribution on Walking Therapy Outcomes in Lower Extremity Artery Disease.
abstract: AIM: To investigate whether angiographic lesion distribution and disease severity influence outcomes of walking therapy in patients with lower extremity artery disease (LEAD) and intermittent claudication (IC). METHODS: In this prospective, single-center cohort study, patients with IC participated in a 12-week hybrid progressive walking program consisting of one supervised treadmill session and two home-based walking sessions per week. Baseline evaluation included assessment of ankle-brachial index (ABI), angiographic imaging (CTA or MRA), and functional exercise testing. Pain-free walking distance (PFWD) and maximal walking distance (MWD) were assessed using standardized treadmill protocols. Angiographic lesion distribution was classified according to lesion location, while disease severity was graded using the ANGIO score. RESULTS: Thirty-three patients (mean age 69.1 ± 9.4 years, 75.8% male) with available angiographic imaging were included in the present analysis. After three months, PFWD increased from 173 m to 304 m, an increase of 131 m (p < 0.001), and MWD increased from 448 m to 627 m, an increase of 179 m (p < 0.001). Lesion distribution was not significantly associated with changes in PFWD (p = 0.059), and no statistically significant differences were observed for MWD (p = 0.44). Disease severity, expressed by the ANGIO score, was not correlated with walking improvements (ρ = -0.10, p = 0.57 for PFWD; ρ = 0.10, p = 0.56 for MWD). CONCLUSION: Walking therapy significantly improved walking capacity in patients with LEAD. In this exploratory cohort, no statistically significant associations were observed between angiographic lesion distribution or disease severity and improvements in walking distance. However, the small overall sample size and limited number of patients within several lesion distribution groups preclude firm conclusions regarding the influence of lesion characteristics on treatment response. These findings should therefore be considered hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in larger studies.

METHODS: In this prospective, single-center cohort study, patients with IC participated in a 12-week hybrid progressive walking program consisting of one supervised treadmill session and two home-based walking sessions per week. Baseline evaluation included assessment of ankle-brachial index (ABI), angiographic imaging (CTA or MRA), and functional exercise testing.

title: One-Year Sac Regression After Endovascular Aneurysm Repair Is Not Always Associated With Favorable Outcomes.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after EVAR indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression. METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent non-ruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020. All patients were stratified into three groups based on their 1-year sac behavior: sac regression (decrease in diameter of ≥ 5mm), stable sac (<5mm change), and sac expansion (increase in diameter of ≥ 5mm). The primary outcome was late re-intervention, including endovascular re-intervention and open conversion. RESULTS: A total of 317 patients were enrolled based on sac status on 1-year follow-up imaging: 126 with sac regression, 177 with stable sacs, and 14 with sac expansion. Over a median follow-up of 69.5 months, sac expansion was a significant risk factor for late re-intervention compared to sac regression (HR, 2.335; 95% CI, 1.048 - 5.191; P=0.047). However, the rate of late re-intervention was not significantly lower in the sac regression group compared to the stable sac group (HR, 0.694; 95% CI, 0.383 - 1.258; P=0.229). Among patients with sac regression at 1 year, 5.6% (7/126) required embolization due to endoleak, and 3.2% (4/126) needed open conversions. CONCLUSION: Late re-intervention rates did not differ significantly between patients with stable versus regressed sacs at 1 year. Patients with sac regression also require regular imaging surveillance to detect late complications.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after EVAR indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression. METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent non-ruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020.

title: Early Morphological Changes in Superficial Varicose Veins After Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To quantify early changes in untreated varicose tributaries and treated saphenous veins after isolated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and to assess 3-month technical outcomes. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n=120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n=13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months. The same radiologist reassessed the anatomically documented site. We used paired analyses, bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable analysis of covariance with robust standard errors. RESULTS: Median tributary diameter decreased from 14.2 mm (IQR, 10.5-21.0) to 11.0 mm (IQR, 7.4-14.2). The median within-patient reduction was 3.0 mm (IQR, 0.9-5.8; 95% bootstrap CI, 2.2-3.7; p<0.001). Completion DUS confirmed closure of the proximal treated saphenous segment and patency of the adjacent deep vein in all patients. At approximately 3 months, complete occlusion was present in 99 of 120 GSVs (82.5%) and all 13 SSVs. The remaining 21 GSVs had short-segment partial recanalization with residual reflux near the saphenofemoral junction; none had complete recanalization. In an exploratory adjusted analysis, diabetes mellitus was associated with a 1.15-mm larger 3-month GSV diameter (95% CI, 0.23-2.07; p=0.015). CONCLUSIONS: Isolated RFA was associated with an early reduction in untreated varicose tributary diameter. These anatomical findings suggest that reassessment before adjunctive tributary treatment may be reasonable; however, clinical benefit cannot be inferred without patient-reported outcomes. The association between diabetes and 3-month GSV diameter is hypothesis-generating.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n=120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n=13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months.

title: Antiplatelet Therapy and Bleeding, Thrombosis, and Aneurysm Growth in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Recent guidelines recommend considering antiplatelet therapy (class IIb recommendation) for patients with AAAs, but bleeding risk remains a concern. This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs. METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed. Demographics and outcomes were compared by antiplatelet status, and multivariable regression identified factors associated with mortality, MACE, bleeding, and AAA growth. RESULTS: Among 886 (73% male) patients studied, 511 (57.7%) were prescribed antiplatelet therapy. Those prescribed antiplatelet therapy had higher rates of atherosclerotic disease than those not on antiplatelets. Patients not prescribed antiplatelet therapy were more likely to be female, have atrial fibrillation, and be prescribed anticoagulation. At a mean follow-up of 1.8 years, there were no differences in bleeding, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism events, or growth rate associated with antiplatelet prescription. Adjusted analyses showed statins (HR=0.73, p=0.02), but not antiplatelets or anticoagulants, were associated with reduced risk of mortality. Diabetes was associated with decreased AAA growth rate, while larger initial diameter was associated with increased growth rate as well as mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with AAA, antiplatelet therapy was not observed to be associated with an increase in bleeding risk, but was also not associated with decreased mortality, thrombosis, or aneurysm growth. Statins were observed to be associated with reduced mortality. Aneurysmal growth rate was not associated with any medical therapies studied, including statins, and was only influenced by the presence of diabetes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Recent guidelines recommend considering antiplatelet therapy (class IIb recommendation) for patients with AAAs, but bleeding risk remains a concern. This study aims to investigate the association of antiplatelet therapy with bleeding, thrombosis, and aneurysm growth among patients with AAAs. METHODS: A single-center retrospective chart review of patients with AAA identified on imaging (2019-2023) was performed.

title: Early and midterm outcomes of the Gore Excluder Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis within and outside the instructions for use for aortoiliac and iliac artery aneurysms.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate perioperative and midterm outcomes of endovascular aneurysm repair using the Gore Excluder Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis (IBE) for aortoiliac and iliac artery aneurysms treated within and outside the instructions for use (IFU). METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent IBE implantation for non-ruptured aortoiliac or iliac artery aneurysms between April 2017 and December 2022. Outcomes were analyzed at the patient, procedure, or IBE-treated-side level, as appropriate. The primary endpoints were technical success, IBE-related complications, and reinterventions. Secondary endpoints included internal iliac artery (IIA) branch patency, aneurysm sac status, and freedom from reintervention or aneurysm-related death. RESULTS: A total of 56 unique patients underwent 58 procedures involving 73 IBE-treated sides; 24 sides were within-IFU and 49 were outside-IFU. Technical success was achieved in 100% of within-IFU procedures and 95.0% of outside-IFU procedures. At 36 months, freedom from reintervention was 79.1% and 94.0% in the within-IFU and outside-IFU groups, respectively (P = .24), and IIA branch patency was 88.8% and 85.5%, respectively. No significant between-group difference in IIA branch patency was detected after accounting for within-patient clustering (hazard ratio, 1.53; 95% confidence interval, 0.28-8.35; P = .62). Seven IIA branch occlusions occurred during follow-up, none of which was associated with buttock claudication. In exploratory univariable analysis, type II endoleak was associated with CIA aneurysm sac growth (odds ratio, 7.86; 95% confidence interval, 1.08-57.0; P = .04). CONCLUSIONS: IBE use outside the IFU was feasible in carefully selected patients. No significant differences in midterm clinical outcomes were detected between the within-IFU and outside-IFU groups.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent IBE implantation for non-ruptured aortoiliac or iliac artery aneurysms between April 2017 and December 2022. Outcomes were analyzed at the patient, procedure, or IBE-treated-side level, as appropriate.

title: Long-term outcomes after angioarchitecture-based endovascular treatment of cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas: a single-center cohort study from Germany.
abstract: PURPOSE: Endovascular treatment is an established option for cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs), and its efficacy has been demonstrated in single-center and multicenter cohorts. In this study, we critically evaluate our single-center experience with a standardized endovascular treatment strategy, assessing angiographic success, recurrence, safety, and long-term outcomes. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients treated endovascularly for cranial dAVFs from January 2014 to October 2019 at the Institute for Neuroradiology, University Hospital Frankfurt, Germany; direct carotid-cavernous fistulas were excluded. Fistulas were Cognard-classified, cavernous-sinus dAVFs additionally Barrow-classified. Treatment was based on angioarchitecture and accessibility, using transarterial liquid embolization and/or transvenous coils. Outcomes included angiographic success, complications, recurrence/retreatment, and symptom evolution from records, follow-up, and structured telephone interviews; median patient-reported clinical follow-up was 53 months. RESULTS: Fifty-five patients were included. Cognard I/ IIa/ IIa + b/ IIb/ III/ IV/ V distribution was 6/10/1/13/16/8/1; 39/55 were high-grade. Definite venous/sinus thrombosis was documented in 22. Initial hemorrhage occurred in 9 and was associated with high-risk drainage (8/22 vs 1/33; p=0.0017) and high-grade Cognard lesions (9/39 vs 0/16; p=0.046). Embolization achieved complete occlusion in 49 cases; three additional patients had residual Cognard type I shunting, resulting in angiographic success in 52/55 patients. One recurrence, three clinical complications, and one technical complication occurred. Patient-reported improvement occurred in 46/50; tinnitus improved most, whereas diplopia persisted in 2/6 cases. CONCLUSION: This single-center study provides a real-world evaluation of our institutional treatment strategy. Our findings support its feasibility, while the small, heterogeneous cohort limits broader conclusions regarding treatment efficacy and durability.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: Endovascular treatment is an established option for cranial dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs), and its efficacy has been demonstrated in single-center and multicenter cohorts. In this study, we critically evaluate our single-center experience with a standardized endovascular treatment strategy, assessing angiographic success, recurrence, safety, and long-term outcomes. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients treated endovascularly for cranial dAVFs from January 2014 to October 2019 at the Institute for Neuroradiology, University Hospital Frankfurt, Germany; direct carotid-cavernous fistulas were excluded.

title: Intraoperative Estimated Blood Loss and Perioperative Transfusion are Independently Associated with Postoperative Morbidity and Mortality After Lower Extremity Bypass.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite endpoint. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion. RESULTS: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 1.26, 95% CI [1.01, 1.59]), myocardial infarction (AOR 1.88, 95% CI [1.48, 2.39]), stroke (AOR 1.58, 95% CI [1.09, 2.29]), and the composite outcome (AOR 1.51, 95% CI [1.29, 1.78]). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (AOR 2.46, 95% CI [1.95, 3.10]), myocardial infarction (AOR 6.57, 95% CI [5.26, 8.21]), stroke (AOR 2.75, 95% CI [1.84, 4.12]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.08, 95% CI [3.48, 4.78]). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (AOR 2.54, 95% CI [2.09, 3.08]), myocardial infarction (AOR 7.39, 95% CI [6.08, 8.98]), stroke (AOR 3.79, 95% CI [2.76, 5.21]), and the composite outcome (AOR 4.42, 95% CI [3.87, 5.05]). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion. CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.
