title: Signal of venous thromboembolism with ethinyl estradiol vs natural estrogens in oral contraceptives: analysis of the EudraVigilance and Food and Drug Administration Adverse Events Reporting System databases.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Disproportionality analyses in the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Events Reporting System (FAERS) and EudraVigilance reported lower reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) with natural estrogen-based combined oral contraceptives (COCs) than with ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel. However, using ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel as the reference showed reduced reporting only for natural estrogen-based products. We therefore reanalyzed both databases separately, using natural estrogen-based COCs as the reference. METHODS: 2 Previously extracted individual case safety report datasets and published disproportionality analyses were re-examined, using natural estrogen-based contraceptives as the comparator. Proportional reporting ratios (PRRs) were recalculated separately for each database. COCs were categorized as ethinylestradiol-based or natural estrogen-based formulations. Drospirenone-only pills were included for comparison. Analyses used pooled natural estrogen contraceptives, estetrol/drospirenone, or estradiol/dienogest as reference groups. Disproportionality was defined as PRR >2, at least 3 cases, and χ≥ 4. DISCUSSION: Consistent patterns were observed in EudraVigilance and FAERS. Compared with natural estrogen-based COCs, ethinylestradiol-based COCs showed a disproportionate reporting of VTE (EudraVigilance: PRR, 5.10 [95% CI, 4.68-5.56]; FAERS: PRR, 4.21 [95% CI, 3.49-5.08]). In EudraVigilance, when using estetrol/drospirenone as the reference, all ethinylestradiol-based formulations showed disproportionality according to the conventional PRR threshold. A similar trend was noted in FAERS, though not statistically significant, with the drospirenone-only formulation comparable to estetrol/drospirenone. CONCLUSION: This analysis revealed a consistent and disproportionate reporting of VTE associated with ethinylestradiol-based COCs compared with natural estrogen-based alternatives across 2 pharmacovigilance databases. These results, together with prior biological and observational research, support further reevaluation of COC options given the estrogenic component's potential influence on VTE risk.

However, using ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel as the reference showed reduced reporting only for natural estrogen-based products. We therefore reanalyzed both databases separately, using natural estrogen-based COCs as the reference.

title: Libman-Sacks Endocarditis as the First Presentation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus in a Young Man: A Multisystemic Diagnostic Challenge.
abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a complex, phenotypically varied disorder that possesses wide-ranging cardiac involvement. Libman-Sacks endocarditis (LSE) is one such cardiac manifestation, which results from the deposition of verrucous, sessile lesions favoring the left-sided heart valves. LSE is typically clinically silent without significant valvular dysfunction. Such patients with LSE, however, are those most susceptible to a more severe clinical phenotype resulting from SLE. Here, we report a unique case of a 22-year-old man initially presenting with unilateral leg swelling found to be secondary to a deep-vein thrombosis. He subsequently developed a constellation of acute symptoms, including embolic strokes, splenic infarction, proteinuric kidney injury, and significant mitral regurgitation, all of which mimicked bacterial endocarditis. His complex, multi-systemic disease course presented diagnostic challenges. We highlight the need in such complex cases for a specialist-led multidisciplinary approach, including cardiologists and rheumatologists, to guide serological and radiological investigations. Early use of echocardiography, in particular 3D transesophageal imaging, was paramount in clinching the diagnosis of LSE as an index presentation of SLE and in the transition from intravenous antibiotics to immunosuppression. Our case underscores the importance of the multidisciplinary team and the role of echocardiography in identifying such patients with LSE in SLE and thereby those most vulnerable to significant end-organ sequelae.

title: When Diabetes Mimics Scleroderma: Cheiroarthropathy and Neuropathic Digital Erosions in Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: Diabetic cheiroarthropathy is an underrecognized complication of diabetes characterized by limited finger joint extension and thickened, waxy skin of the hands. It can clinically mimic several rheumatologic conditions, particularly systemic sclerosis, creating a diagnostic challenge. We report the case of a 68-year-old man with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus who presented with hand stiffness and contractures, scleroderma-like skin thickening, and nonpainful crusted digital erosions, raising concern for systemic sclerosis-associated digital ulceration. He underwent rheumatologic evaluation and received immunosuppressive therapy without improvement in the cutaneous findings, prompting further clinical reassessment. His overall clinical phenotype, including a positive prayer sign, skin thickening confined to the digits, absence of Raynaud phenomenon, normal nailfold capillaries, and negative anti-Scl-70 and anticentromere antibodies, favored diabetic cheiroarthropathy over systemic sclerosis. The digital erosions were considered likely multifactorial, with contributions from unrecognized trauma in the setting of diabetic neuropathy and possible vascular compromise related to peripheral arterial disease and tobacco use. This case highlights the clinical overlap between diabetic cheiroarthropathy and systemic sclerosis, particularly when digital erosions accompany scleroderma-like hand changes. Recognizing this presentation may help prevent misdiagnosis and unnecessary immunosuppression while directing management toward glycemic control, prevention of repetitive trauma, local wound care, and occupational therapy.

title: Short-Term Outcomes of Lower-Extremity Surgical Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Among Yemeni Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of amputation and mortality. We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen. We enrolled 39 consecutive adults with CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) who were selected for and considered fit to undergo open lower-extremity surgical revascularization between December 2022 and September 2024; follow-up was completed in December 2024. The study protocol was reviewed and approved by the Al-Thawra Hospital Ethics Committee (approval no. 33-2026), and written informed consent was obtained from all participants. The study was not registered. This was an exploratory consecutive cohort; no formal sample-size calculation was performed, and no contemporaneous endovascular, nonoperative, or primary-amputation comparator group was included. Primary endpoints were graft patency and limb salvage at three months. Secondary outcomes were secondary patency, postoperative complications, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) and Vascular Quality of Life Questionnaire-6 (VascuQoL-6) scores. Paired comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical comparisons. RESULTS: The mean age was 60.9 years (SD 9.7), and 30 patients (76.9%) were male. Diabetes mellitus and hypertension were present in 34 (87.2%) and 30 (76.9%) patients, respectively. Nineteen patients (48.7%) had ischemic rest pain, and 20 (51.3%) had tissue loss. Great saphenous vein (GSV) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) grafts were used in 28 (71.8%) and 11 (28.2%) patients, respectively. At three months, primary patency was 84.6% (33/39 grafts; 95% CI 70.3%-92.8%), secondary patency was 89.7% (35/39 grafts; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%), and limb salvage was 89.7% (35/39 patients; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%). Given the small cohort, the confidence intervals around these estimates were relatively wide. Among the 35 patients with limb preservation, mean ABI increased from 0.35 (SD 0.11) to 0.55 (SD 0.12; mean difference 0.21, 95% CI 0.19-0.23; p<0.001), and mean VascuQoL-6 score increased from 10.3 (SD 2.9) to 16.6 (SD 4.0; mean difference 6.3, 95% CI 5.6-7.1; p<0.001). Complications occurred in nine patients (23.1%). In an exploratory unadjusted subgroup analysis, GSV use was associated with higher primary patency than PTFE use (92.9% vs 63.6%, p=0.042). CONCLUSION: In this single-center prospective cohort, open surgical revascularization was feasible and was associated with 89.7% limb salvage and 84.6% primary patency at three months. Improvements in ABI and VascuQoL-6 were observed among patients with limb preservation. Autologous GSV use was associated with higher primary patency; this finding requires confirmation in larger, adjusted studies.

METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen.

title: Association of the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index with Ascending Aortic Diameter and Dilatation: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives Materials and Methods n n Results p p p p Conclusions : Complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices are inexpensive and widely available, but data on their relationship with ascending aortic size are limited. This study examined the association between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and ascending aortic diameter, and compared these indices according to the presence of ascending aortic dilatation (AAD) defined by a 40 mm threshold.: In this single-centre retrospective cross-sectional study, 251 patients aged 18 years or older (mean age, 53.1 ± 16.7 years; range, 18-95 years; 160 men) who underwent thoracic computed tomography angiography were grouped by maximum tubular ascending aortic diameter (<40 mm,= 158; ≥40 mm,= 93). Inference for the primary linear model was based on heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors. Height and weight were not recorded, so the models could not be adjusted for body size.: In unadjusted comparisons, platelet and neutrophil counts, creatinine and all five inflammatory indices were nominally higher in the dilated group (all< 0.05), whereas C-reactive protein did not differ. In the primary adjusted model, each 100-unit increase in SII was associated with a 0.59 mm greater ascending aortic diameter (HC3 95% CI 0.28 to 0.90; β = 0.197;< 0.001), approximately 1.6 mm across the interquartile range of SII; the model explained 26.9% of the variance. Higher SII was also associated with AAD in the secondary logistic model (odds ratio per 100 units, 1.34; 95% CI 1.17 to 1.53;< 0.001). Discrimination was weak (area under the curve for SII, 0.658; 95% CI 0.590 to 0.726); the sample-derived cut-off gave a positive likelihood ratio of 1.38, and its 2.5-97.5th percentile interval on bootstrap internal validation was 305 to 579. None of the 75 correlations survived false discovery rate adjustment, and the SII-by-sex interaction was not significant (= 0.621).: Higher SII was associated with a greater ascending aortic diameter and with the presence of AAD after adjustment for the measured covariates; because body size could not be accounted for, residual confounding cannot be excluded. The adjusted difference was modest and discrimination was weak. These findings do not support the use of SII as a standalone diagnostic marker for ascending aortic dilatation.

title: Integrated Analysis of Serotonin-Related Biomarkers in Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Based on Machine Learning and Single-Cell Sequencing Data.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Serotonin, as an important neurotransmitter and signaling molecule, can affect thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) by regulating vascular cell proliferation, angiogenesis, and immune status. This research aimed to conduct a comprehensive analysis to pinpoint serotonin-related biomarkers in TAA and to elucidate their potential molecular mechanisms.Biomarkers were selected and validated through differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning algorithms, and expression verification. Moreover, the constructed nomogram, enrichment analysis, immune infiltration analysis, and compound prediction validated the regulatory roles of the biomarkers in TAA. The single-cell dataset was analyzed to determine key cells and perform pseudo-time analysis. Simulated knockout of biomarkers was performed to determine their underlying functions and related pathways. Finally, reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was employed to confirm the expression levels of the biomarkers.Overall, two biomarkers (CD300A and CLU) were determined to be associated with serotonin in TAA. The nomogram showed good performance in predicting TAA risk. These biomarkers were significantly enriched in the hematopoietic cell lineage and natural killer (NK) cell mediated cytotoxicity. Biomarker expression was significantly correlated with the infiltration proportions of M2 macrophages and neutrophils. The biomarkers were stably bound to tetrachlorodibenzodioxin and bisphenol A. Moreover, pseudo-time analysis demonstrated a notable correlation between biomarker expression and the differentiation status of monocytes/macrophages/dendritic cells (MonoMac/DC). Genes perturbed by knockout were enriched in the pyrimidine metabolism and RIG-I-like receptor signaling pathway. Finally, RT-qPCR validated that CLU was downregulated and CD300A was upregulated in the TAA group.Biomarkers (CD300A and CLU) associated with serotonin in TAA were identified, with their expression trends validated by RT-qPCR. This work provides novel bioinformatic insights, and direct functional experiments are required to support future therapeutic development for TAA.

title: Transcatheter Electrosurgical Aortic Septotomy Across the Spectrum of Type B Aortic Dissection: Feasibility, Technical Lessons, and Bailout Strategies.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter electrosurgical aortic septotomy (TEAS) has been introduced to optimise luminal geometry during endovascular repair of complex type B aortic dissection (TBAD), but data across dissection phases and on complication management remain limited. This study reports early outcomes, quantitative common lumen creation, and bailout strategies from a consecutive single centre experience. METHOD: Eight consecutive patients underwent TEAS, between December 2024 and January 2026, as an adjunct to thoracic endovascular aortic repair or physician modified fenestrated endograft for acute, subacute, or chronic TBAD, including post-type A repair and genetic aortopathy. Pre-procedural and follow up computed tomography angiography (CTA) quantified true lumen and common lumen cross sectional area. Septotomy technical success, peri-operative outcomes, complications, and early follow up were assessed. RESULTS: 2 2 The mean age was 51.1 ± 17 years; five were men. Two patients were acute, two subacute, and four chronic; two had Marfan syndrome, both redo cases after previous open repair. Septotomy technical success was 100%. The median cross sectional area increased from 174.5 mm(pre-procedural true lumen) to 1 007 mm(follow up CTA common lumen) after TEAS (5.3 fold increase). There were no 30 day, in hospital, or aortic related deaths. Three major procedure related complications (38%) occurred, all in non-acute cases and all managed endovascularly: one iliac lamellar dislodgement requiring kissing stents, one external iliac rupture treated with stent grafting, and one delayed superior mesenteric artery occlusion managed with stenting. All acute cases were uneventful. Median clinical follow up was 32 days (range 22 - 308) and median imaging follow up was 20 days (range 2 - 265), with no late deaths, no aortic re-interventions, and no aneurysmal dilatation of the non-stented TEAS treated segment. CONCLUSION: TEAS may be considered across acute, subacute, and chronic TBAD, including redo and connective tissue disease cases, enabling reproducible common lumen creation and landing zone optimisation. All complications were recognised and managed endovascularly and were observed only in non-acute dissections, although the sample size precluded meaningful assessment of any relationship between dissection phase and technical risk. These findings support TEAS as a feasible adjunct in carefully selected complex dissections, offer practical principles for safe adoption, and reflect an early experience that may be influenced by the learning curve of this technically demanding procedure.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify CCR2-Dependent Monocyte-Smooth Muscle Cell Crosstalk in Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Aortic aneurysm (AA) involves inflammatory recruitment and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) remodeling, but the cellular contribution of candidate chemokine receptors remains unclear. We prioritized reproducible AA-associated genes, localized their cellular sources, and tested whether monocyte CCR2 influences human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs). METHODS: Differentially expressed genes shared by GSE57691 and GSE7084 underwent enrichment, protein-protein interaction, regulatory-network, and drug-gene analyses. Hub genes were assessed in GSE9106 and localized in GSE166676 single-cell RNA-sequencing data. CCR2-silenced THP-1 monocytic cells were indirectly co-cultured with HASMCs. CCR2 knockdown was verified by quantitative PCR; HASMC remodeling-related proteins and 24-h scratch-wound closure were evaluated. RESULTS: p p p We identified 107 common upregulated genes and ten immune-related hubs. CCR2 was monocyte-enriched and higher in AA cells overall (= 0.00799) and AA monocytes (= 0.00440). THP-1 co-culture increased COL3A1 and SPP1, decreased α-SMA and TPM, and increased HASMC wound closure. CCR2 silencing partially reversed these changes and decreased wound closure versus siNC-THP-1 cells (< 0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Multi-omic evidence and non-contact co-culture support CCR2-dependent monocyte-HASMC paracrine crosstalk in AA-associated remodeling. The responsible mediators and in vivo relevance require further study.

title: Cardiovascular and mortality outcomes with JAK versus TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: a target trial emulation (CARDINAL-RA).
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aims to compare cardiovascular and mortality outcomes of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) versus tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) at elevated cardiovascular risk using target trial emulation. METHODS: Within TriNetX, adults with RA aged ≥50 years and ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor initiating JAKi or TNFi were compared in a new-user, active-comparator design. Improved 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, individual conventional synthetic DMARDs, oral corticosteroids, prior non-TNF biologic exposure, and baseline inflammatory markers. The primary outcome was MACE (nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal ischemic stroke); the secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and venous thromboembolism (VTE), with cataract as a prespecified negative control. Follow-up began 90 days after initiation. Cox models estimated hazard ratios, with 5-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidences and absolute risk differences per 1,000. Cohorts were separately matched by agent, sex, cardiovascular-risk stratum, and index era; E-values quantified sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. RESULTS: p In 18,757 matched pairs, JAKi was not associated with excess MACE (HR 1.002, 0.923-1.088; +2.11 per 1,000). All-cause mortality, a secondary outcome, was higher with JAKi (HR 1.158, 1.058-1.268; = 0.0014; +10.4 per 1,000; E-value 1.586), whereas heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.019, 0.955-1.088) and VTE (HR 1.054, 0.961-1.156) did not differ; the negative control showed no excess (HR 0.934, 0.867-1.007). No agent showed a significant excess in MACE or mortality (mortality HR 1.052 tofacitinib, 1.213 baricitinib, and 1.090 upadacitinib); the only nominally significant agent-level finding was VTE with baricitinib (HR 1.364, 1.028-1.809; 198 events). A three-component composite including death was non-significant (HR 1.058, 0.992-1.127). No consistent effect modification was seen by sex, cardiovascular risk burden, or index year. CONCLUSION: JAKi initiation was not associated with excess MACE (primary outcome), heart failure hospitalization, or VTE. A modest excess in all-cause mortality was observed as a secondary outcome, with no signal for any individual agent. This association was of modest robustness (E-value 1.586) and was not reproduced in any agent-specific cohort, so residual channeling bias cannot be excluded. The null MACE result should not be read as class-wide cardiovascular safety reassurance nor the mortality signal as an established causal effect.

title: Drug-Eluting Resorbable Scaffolds for Infrapopliteal Peripheral Artery Disease: A State-of-the-Art Review.
abstract: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD. Most recently, randomized evidence from the LIFE-BTK trial has demonstrated superior patency and reduced rates of revascularization with DRS-treated lesions as compared with plain balloon angioplasty. In this state-of-the-art review, we summarize the existing evidence evaluating DRS devices for BTK PAD and present an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of clinical outcomes for DRS-based endovascular interventions.
englishSummary: Drug-eluting resorbable scaffolds (DRS) have been developed to overcome the key limitations of conventional endovascular therapies for below-the-knee (BTK) peripheral artery disease (PAD), including acute recoil, restenosis, and the sequela of long-term permanent metallic implants. DRS provides a temporary mechanical support and localized antiproliferative drug delivery after which the scaffold is gradually resorbed, ultimately restoring native vessel architecture to preserve future revascularization options. Over the past decade, numerous prospective and observational studies have evaluated both polymer- and magnesium alloy-based DRS platforms and have demonstrated favorable patency, wound healing, and limb salvage outcomes in patients with advanced infrapopliteal PAD.

title: Changes in Stroke Care Regionalization in California Associated With Evolving Evidence of Benefit for Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Network Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2015 demonstration of the benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) led to increases in interhospital transfer of patients with large vessel occlusion stroke. We sought to characterize the associated evolution in stroke care regionalization. METHODS: We used comprehensive California statewide all-payer administrative data from 2010 to 2021 to identify ischemic stroke encounters and transfers (using recorded disposition and adjacent claims). We applied network analysis methods to create the interhospital transfer network, examine access to EVT-capable hospitals (time-varying, based on performance of ≥2 EVT cases that year), and used block models to identify clusters of hospitals closely connected through transfer by year and pre- versus post-2015. We used regression modeling with a linear spline and knot at 2015 to examine changes in network characteristics over time. RESULTS: We identified 19 244 transfers between 338 hospitals. Pre-2015, 7 of 11 clusters had ≥1 EVT-capable hospital. Post-2015, 24 of 26 clusters had ≥1 EVT-capable hospital. More hospitals had EVT capability over time (21.6% [70/324] to 33.7% [106/315]). EVT-capable hospitals consistently received more transferred patients relative to noncapable hospitals (mean number of received transfers/y pre-2015: 55.2 versus 15.6; post-2015: 97.3 versus 13.8). Initially, transfers for EVT increased from 10.7% of EVT cases having an interhospital transfer in 2010 to 36.0% by 2016. After 2016, the trend reversed, decreasing to 21.7% by 2021. CONCLUSIONS: The California stroke system of care became less regionalized for EVT access from 2010 to 2021. Although we expected increased consolidation with fewer clusters centered around EVT-capable hospitals, we instead observed an increased number of EVT-capable hospitals with more clusters around them and less need for transfer to access EVT. More work is needed to examine the relative trade-offs of regionalization patterns in stroke systems of care, given recognized benefits of more regionalized care around higher-volume centers in other conditions.

title: Reevaluating hypercoagulability in the portal vein and the impact of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt on platelet activation in cirrhosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In liver cirrhosis, dysregulated hemostasis predisposes patients to both hemorrhagic and thrombotic complications. The portal vein (PV) is a frequent site of thrombosis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Whether the PV constitutes a locally hypercoagulable environment remains controversial, as previous studies have reported conflicting findings regarding portal venous platelet activation, endothelial dysfunction, and coagulation factor alterations. METHODS: We enrolled 34 patients with liver cirrhosis undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) implantation. Platelet count, activation, and reactivity were assessed by flow cytometry before and after TIPS, as well as across multiple vascular compartments, including the PV, superior mesenteric vein, hepatic vein, and peripheral vein. In addition, we measured key coagulation factors involved in secondary hemostasis in the indicated vessels. RESULTS: Platelet counts declined with advancing liver disease, but no changes in platelet activation or reactivity were observed. Despite elevated platelet counts in the PV, we found no evidence of increased platelet activation or reactivity. Moreover, no compartment-specific differences were detected in the selected conventional coagulation parameters assessed, except for lower fibrinogen levels in the PV compared with the hepatic vein. TIPS implantation did not lead to a short-term increase in platelet activation. CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, we found no evidence of increased portal venous platelet activation or reactivity. Apart from lower fibrinogen levels in the PV compared with the hepatic vein, the selected conventional coagulation parameters assessed did not show consistent compartment-specific differences. These findings do not support the concept of a PV-specific hypercoagulable state as assessed by the present platelet activation and reactivity measures and selected coagulation assays. Rather, they suggest that relief of portal hypertension and reduction of venous stasis may be more relevant for thrombosis risk than changes in platelet activation alone.

title: Acute-on-Chronic Limb Ischemia Mimicking Cellulitis: A Diagnostic Pitfall.
abstract: Acute-on-chronic limb ischemia may present with clinical features that overlap with inflammatory conditions, potentially delaying recognition of arterial compromise. We report a case of an elderly woman with long-standing polycythemia treated with hydroxyurea who presented with progressive right foot pain, marked swelling, erythema, tenderness, and bluish discoloration of the hallux. She was discharged from the emergency department but returned the next night with worsening pain. Soft-tissue ultrasonography demonstrated diffuse subcutaneous edema without a localized collection, supporting an initial provisional diagnosis of cellulitis. Despite preserved motor function and sensation, progressive ischemic discoloration, prolonged capillary refill, and abnormal distal pulse findings prompted further vascular assessment. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 6.2-cm right popliteal arterial thrombus with impaired distal perfusion. Her D-dimer was within the laboratory reference range at 0.40 µg/mL FEU, while the hematocrit was markedly elevated at 55.3%. Intravenous unfractionated heparin was initiated, resulting in improvement in pain and swelling and clinical stabilization, while definitive revascularization options were considered. The patient subsequently elected to pursue definitive treatment in her home country, precluding assessment of long-term limb-salvage outcomes. This case emphasizes the importance of careful and repeated vascular assessment in a painful, discolored limb, particularly before neuromotor deficits develop. Laboratory findings, including D-dimer, should be interpreted within their validated clinical context and should not supersede clinical evidence of impaired arterial perfusion.

She was discharged from the emergency department but returned the next night with worsening pain.

title: Blue Toe Syndrome and Acute Kidney Injury Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Biopsy-Proven Case of Cholesterol Embolization Syndrome.
abstract: Cholesterol embolization syndrome (CES) is an underrecognized complication of arterial instrumentation caused by embolization of atheromatous debris into small- and medium-sized arteries. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is well described after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), but biopsy-proven CES after TAVR is rarely reported. Its delayed presentation may be mistaken for contrast-associated nephropathy, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, or systemic vasculitis. A 77-year-old man with chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and peripheral artery disease underwent transfemoral TAVR for severe aortic stenosis. Preprocedural computed tomography angiography showed a "shaggy aorta." One month later, he developed intermittent, painless violaceous discoloration of the left first through third toes. Approximately 2.5 months after TAVR, serum creatinine had risen from a baseline of 1.2-1.5 mg/dL to 4.24 mg/dL, prompting admission. Microscopic hematuria, mild eosinophilia (0.64 ×10³/µL), elevated inflammatory markers, and dysmorphic erythrocytes raised concern for glomerulonephritis and vasculitis, and empiric intravenous methylprednisolone was given while diagnostic evaluation proceeded. Kidney biopsy demonstrated atheroembolic cholesterol clefts in intrarenal arteries with ischemic changes, without glomerulonephritis or immune complex deposition. Preserved pedal pulses with an ankle-brachial index of 1.21 and toe-brachial index of 0.98 supported distal microembolization rather than large-vessel occlusion. Corticosteroids were stopped, nephrotoxins withheld, aspirin resumed, and high-intensity statin therapy was initiated; creatinine improved to approximately 3.1 mg/dL by discharge. CES should remain in the differential for progressive AKI with blue toe syndrome after TAVR, even when presentation is delayed, and initial findings suggest immune-mediated disease.

title: Venous thromboembolism in patients with distant-stage uterine cancer: a comparison of primary cytoreductive surgery versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence and temporal distribution of venous thromboembolism in patients with distant-stage uterine cancer treated with primary cytoreductive surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval cytoreductive surgery. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program-Medicare data to identify women aged ≥65 years with Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program Summary Stage distant uterine cancer diagnosed from 2008 to 2017 who underwent both hysterectomy and chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis. Treatment was classified by the sequence of surgery and chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism, comprising pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis, was identified from claims. Patients with baseline venous thromboembolism (6 months before through the month of diagnosis) were excluded from the primary analysis. Cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was estimated using competing risk methods (death as a competing event) and compared via Gray's test. Multi-variable analysis evaluated factors associated with venous thromboembolism during the first 6 months after diagnosis, adjusting for demographic, clinical, and tumor characteristics. Landmark, time-varying treatment-phase, and first-treatment-anchored sensitivity analyses were performed to address immortal time and time-zero misalignment. RESULTS: Of 1977 patients, 186 (9.4%) had venous thromboembolism prior to diagnosis and were excluded, leaving 1791 patients for analysis: 74.7% underwent primary cytoreductive surgery and 25.3% received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy use increased from 17.6% (2008) to 35.5% (2017). Neoadjuvant chemotherapy patients had higher baseline venous thromboembolism prevalence (14.7% vs 7.5%, p<.001) and comorbidity burden. Overall, 568 venous thromboembolism events occurred; cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was 20.1% at 6 months, 33.6% at 24 months, and 49.3% at 60 months. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy patients had higher early cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence (23.0% vs 19.1% at 6 months; 40.8% vs 31.5% at 24 months), with convergence by 60 months (46.5% vs 49.2%; Gray's test p=.054). In multi-variable analysis, the adjusted risk ratio for early venous thromboembolism with neoadjuvant chemotherapy versus primary cytoreductive surgery was 1.21 (95% confidence interval 0.97-1.51), an imprecise estimate that does not exclude a clinically meaningful increase in early risk. CONCLUSIONS: Among older patients with distant-stage uterine cancer, venous thromboembolism was common, affecting approximately 1 in 5 patients within 6 months and nearly 1 in 2 within 5 years. The cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence did not differ significantly between primary cytoreductive surgery and neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Events occurred earlier in the neoadjuvant chemotherapy group, a pattern that may reflect baseline differences between the groups and differential ascertainment as much as treatment sequence. Our findings support the need for a prospective evaluation of treatment-phase-specific thromboprophylaxis.

title: Genetic Patterns in Familial Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: We examined familial patterns and phenotypes of thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections (TAAD) in the 3746 patients currently populating our Yale Aortic Institute Database. METHODS: Patient charts and electronic medical records were retrospectively reviewed for the entire cohort. TAAD disease was categorized as syndromic (with extra-aortic manifestations) or non-syndromic (without) for each patient. Family patterns and whole exome sequencing results were assessed. Family history was considered 'proven' when a patient's relative(s) had an arterial aneurysm or dissection confirmed by an imaging study, surgical treatment, or postmortem examination. Family history was termed 'likely' when at least one relative suffered sudden death at ages ≤50 for males and ≤60 for females, and 'possible' with a history of sudden death at any age. RESULTS: p p p p Of the 3746 patients in the database, family history of aneurysm or dissection and connective tissue status was able to be determined for 3113 patients, divided into 109 (3.5%) syndromic and 3004 (96.5%) non-syndromic TAAD patients. Findings were as follows: (1) In the syndromic group, 46 (42.2%) patients had a 'proven' family history, 6 (5.5%) had a 'likely' family history, 4 (3.7%) had a 'possible' family history, and 18 (16.5%) had 'none'. For 35 patients (32.1%) their family history was unknown. (2) In the non-syndromic group, 587 (19.5%) patients had 'proven' family history, 147 (4.9%) had 'likely' family history, 210 (7.0%) had 'possible' family history and 1444 (48.1%) had no family history, thus representing sporadic TAAD. A total of 616 (20.5%) had an unknown family history. (3) There was a significant difference between the rate for 'proven' and 'none' family history between the syndromic and non-syndromic groups (42.2% vs. 19.5% and 16.5% vs. 48.1%, respectively;< 0.001). (4) Syndromic patients presented at a significantly younger age than non-syndromic or sporadic patients (41.2 vs. 63.3 or 63.6;< 0.001). (5) There was no significant difference in age of presentation between familial non-syndromic (patients with 'proven', 'likely', and 'possible' family history) and sporadic patients (63.3 vs. 63.6;= 0.64). (6) Overall, of the 3746 patients in the database, 631 patients (25 syndromic, 552 non-syndromic, and 54 with unknown status) underwent Whole Exome Sequencing (WES). Sequencing revealed 170 disease-causing or suspicious variants [13 pathogenic, 16 likely pathogenic, 7 not classified, and 134 Variants of Uncertain Significance (VUS)] found in the exomes of 141 (22.3%) patients (12 syndromic, 103 non-syndromic TAAD patients plus a remaining 26 of unknown connective tissue status). Seventy (49.6%) of these patients had a 'proven' family history. (7) Familial TAAD patients were more likely to find a variant in their WES result than patients without a family history (70 vs. 26;< 0.001). Recognition of these strong familial patterns, even in non-syndromic cases, encourages intensive investigation of family in order to save lives by detecting silent TAA disease. CONCLUSIONS: Our large-scale, clinical and sequencing-based study clearly demonstrates the strongly familial and genetically mediated nature of thoracic aortic disease. We vividly demonstrate and characterize this familial nature of TAAD, both clinically and by genetic sequencing. Our findings strongly support vigorous family investigation when a new patient is diagnosed with thoracic aortic aneurysm, as well as vigorous application of whole exome sequencing for these families.

title: Anatomical Predictors of Endovascular Technical Success in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: The Role of GLASS and Diabetes.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: n n p p p p p p Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is associated with high rates of major adverse limb events and mortality, particularly in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS) standardizes anatomical assessment and supports revascularization planning. This study evaluated the association of anatomical complexity and diabetes with immediate technical success after infrainguinal endovascular treatment.This single-center retrospective study included 136 patients undergoing infrainguinal endovascular procedures for CLTI between May 2021 and May 2023, stratified into diabetic (= 85) and non-diabetic (= 51) groups. Anatomical complexity was assessed using GLASS. Technical success was defined as restoration of inline flow to the foot. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed.Technical success was achieved in 74.3% of procedures, without significant differences between diabetic and non-diabetic patients (75.3% vs. 72.5%,= 0.723). Success declined progressively from 86.3% in GLASS stage I to 75.5% in stage II and 53.1% in stage III (= 0.003; trend= 0.001). In multivariable analysis, GLASS FP (femoropopliteal) grade ≥2 (adjusted OR 8.068, 95% CI 3.018-21.562;< 0.001) and tibioperoneal trunk occlusion (adjusted OR 4.874, 95% CI 1.271-18.687;= 0.021) were independently associated with technical failure, whereas diabetes was not. The model showed good discrimination (AUC 0.820, 95% CI 0.744-0.897;< 0.001).Anatomical complexity was associated with immediate technical success in CLTI, whereas no independent association with diabetes was detected in this cohort. GLASS may provide clinically relevant preprocedural risk stratification and support endovascular planning.

title: The Venification of the Artery: Insights from Single-Cell Transcriptomics of a Porcine Arteriovenous Fistula Model.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The maturation of an autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) depends on the coordinated hemodynamic adaptation of the inflow artery and the outflow vein. While venous remodeling has been extensively studied, the mechanisms of arterial adaptation are poorly understood. We addressed this knowledge gap with the first temporal single-cell atlas of the porcine AVF model. METHODS: Six Yorkshire pigs underwent bilateral femoro-femoral AVF creation for tissue harvest at 2 and 21 days postoperatively or sham operation to collect native vessels after 2 days. Arteries and veins were analyzed by droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing, histology, and immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: HEY2, HEYL CCN3, CCN5 DKK2, SFRP4 C3, C7, CFD All fistulas were patent, with flows reaching 1185.0 ± 170.6 mL/min despite mild to moderate neointima formation in the veins. Arteries and veins demonstrated >60% endothelial denudation and increased neovascularization. Arterial remodeling was characterized by a progressive increase in venous-like transcriptional features. Arteries presented a venous-like endothelial cell (EC) composition at 21 days postop and a temporal increase in venous-associated phenotypes of myofibroblasts and fibroblasts. In both vessels, the latter populations were the main bearers of mechanosensitive signatures at 2 days. Despite the temporal convergence in phenotypes, arteries and veins retained vessel-selective characteristics. Arterial ECs expressed high levels of nitric oxide synthase, whereas venous ECs were largely inflammatory. Arterial myofibroblasts and fibroblasts had higher expression of Notch signaling transducers () and cellular communication network factors (), while Wnt signaling regulators () and complement genes () were upregulated in veins. Anti-inflammatory macrophages increased in both vessels during remodeling, likely contributing to the maturation of the fistulas. CONCLUSION: These analyses challenge the traditional paradigm of exclusive vein arterialization and support a complementary process of arterial venification after anastomosis. Recognition of this underappreciated phenomenon may reshape our understanding of AVF biology and guide the discovery of both vascular-wide and vessel-selective anti-stenotic therapies.

title: One-year outcomes of percutaneous deep vein arterialization in the Dutch LimFlow registry.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous deep vein arterialization (pDVA) offers a potential endovascular alternative for reducing the risk of major amputation in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) who have no standard revascularization options "no-option" CLTI (NO-CLTI). METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter registry conducted in the Netherlands between May 2020 and June 2024, patients with NO-CLTI underwent pDVA using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical). The primary end point was amputation-free survival at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included limb salvage, overall survival, patency, pain scores, wound healing, transcutaneous oxygen pressure, and quality of life (QoL). RESULTS: A total of 26 limbs of 23 patients with NO-CLTI (mean age, 64 ± 12 years; 20 men) were included, all classified as Rutherford category 5 and 17 (77.3%) as Wound Ischemia and foot Infection stage 4. Thirteen (53.8%) patients suffered from diabetes mellitus and six (21.7%) from renal insufficiency. Technical success was 100%. Amputation-free survival was 69.2%, limb salvage 80.8%, and overall survival 88.5% at 12 months. Primary patency, primary-assisted patency, and secondary patency rates at 12 months were 6.6%, 27.3%, and 35.7%, respectively. Reinterventions were performed to maintain patency in 85% of the limbs and 58% for maturation of the pDVA. Median time to wound healing was 6.9 months, with 73.4% healed at 12 months. Pain scores decreased significantly (P <.001) in 12 months. QoL improved from a mean of 37% to 68% on the VascuQoL-25, though these analyses were based on limited available data. CONCLUSIONS: pDVA in patients with NO-CLTI is safe and effective at 12 months, preventing major amputation and mortality in the majority of patients. QoL also appeared to improve following pDVA. These observations warrant confirmation in larger studies. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study strengthens existing evidence on the effectivity and safety of percutaneous deep vein arterialization using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical) in patients with "no-option" chronic limb-threatening ischemia. Our data demonstrated a 100% technical success rate and comparable amputation-free survival and limb salvage to other percutaneous deep vein arterialization studies. Notably, this prospective and well-phenotyped cohort uniquely incorporated patient-reported outcome measures, showing improvements in pain, transcutaneous oxygen pressure and quality of life.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter registry conducted in the Netherlands between May 2020 and June 2024, patients with NO-CLTI underwent pDVA using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical). The primary end point was amputation-free survival at 12 months.

title: Cardiovascular involvement in gram-negative bloodstream infection: Timing, phenotypes, and mechanisms.
abstract: Gram-negative bloodstream infection (GN-BSI) is associated with a heterogeneous spectrum of cardiovascular manifestations extending beyond the hemodynamic consequences of sepsis. Epidemiological evidence identifies a transient period of heightened cardiovascular vulnerability, with myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke clustering close to BSI onset, alongside myocardial dysfunction, arrhythmias, thrombotic complications, and direct vascular or endovascular infection. These phenotypes likely reflect different interactions between systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, immunothrombosis, underlying cardiovascular disease, and pathogen-specific factors. Persistent bacteremia, prosthetic cardiovascular material, vascular disease, and selected Gram-negative pathogens may identify settings warranting greater cardiovascular attention. However, current evidence remains limited by predominantly retrospective designs, heterogeneous outcome definitions, non-standardized cardiovascular assessment, and limited integration of microbiological and cardiovascular data. This review integrates clinical, epidemiological, and mechanistic evidence to define the timing, phenotypes, and mechanisms of cardiovascular involvement in GN-BSI and proposes a phenotype-driven framework for cardiovascular interpretation and future research.

title: Deterioration of Peri-Infarct Microvascular Hemodynamics Following Successful Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Predicts Infarct Growth.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion. METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study from the University of California, Los Angeles, patients with acute ischemic stroke from 2015 to 2020 were included if they had excellent reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2c) and diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MRIs at baseline, immediately PT, and 24 to 48 hours after thrombectomy. Peri-infarct regions were defined as time to maximum ≥6-second regions on baseline MRI that were not infarcted on immediate PT MRI. Following image coregistration, quantitative values of perfusion parameters, including RTH, were obtained from peri-infarct regions on immediate PT MRI. Two primary outcomes were assessed: (1) infarct growth ≥10 mL and (2) poor functional outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale score >2). Associations between clinical and imaging parameters and outcomes were evaluated using univariate analysis. Age, sex, and covariates that were significant in univariate analysis were included in logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: P P P P Among 47 patients included in the analysis (62% women; mean age, 72±13 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 14), 20 (43%) patients had substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcome. Peri-infarct RTH was significantly (=0.005) higher in patients with infarct growth >10 mL than those without and remained as an independent predictor (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-2.0];=0.04). Similarly, the peri-infarct RTH was significantly higher (<0.001) in patients with poor functional outcomes than those with good functional outcomes and remained as a significant predictor of poor functional outcome (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-1.9];=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Increased peri-infarct RTH on immediate PT MRI predicts substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcomes in successfully reperfused patients with acute ischemic stroke. Results highlight the role of microvascular dysfunction depicted by elevated RTH as a potential marker of no-reflow phenomenon despite excellent macrovascular reperfusion.

title: Reverse Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Complicated by Neurogenic Pulmonary Edema in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Case Report.
abstract: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TTC) is a recognized and potentially severe cardiac complication in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Reverse TTC (rTTC), a rare variant characterized by basal hypokinesis with apical sparing, is infrequently reported in this setting. The coexistence of rTTC with neurogenic pulmonary edema has not been previously described and represents a complex neurocardiac interaction that can significantly worsen outcomes. We report the case of a previously healthy 30-year-old man who presented with high-grade aSAH secondary to rupture of an anterior communicating artery aneurysm. His course was complicated by neurogenic pulmonary edema, refractory hypoxemia, hemodynamic instability, and rTTC. Management required early airway protection, bronchoscopy, vasopressor support, and complex stent-assisted endovascular coiling. Echocardiography demonstrated reduced left ventricular ejection fraction with basal hypokinesis and apical sparing, consistent with rTTC. Careful hemodynamic management was essential to balance cerebral perfusion against myocardial dysfunction. With multidisciplinary critical care and structured rehabilitation, the patient achieved favorable neurological and functional recovery. This case highlights that rTTC in aSAH is not a benign condition and may be associated with increased morbidity when combined with neurogenic pulmonary edema due to massive catecholamine surge. Early recognition using bedside echocardiography, prompt aneurysm securing, and balanced hemodynamic support are critical for improving outcomes.

title: Single-cell landscape of lymphoid and myeloid heterogeneity across type-stratified craniofacial lesions in polyostotic fibrous dysplasia.
abstract: BACKGROUND: GNAS Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia (POFD) is a mosaic skeletal disorder driven by somaticmutations that constitutively activate Gsα-cAMP signaling, producing fibro-osseous craniofacial deformities. POFD lesions are histologically classified into three subtypes-Type I (connective-tissue predominant), Type II (cancellous-bone predominant), and Type III (sclerotic-bone predominant)-yet the immune microenvironment across these categories remains undefined. This study aims to dissect lymphoid and myeloid heterogeneity and inter-cellular communication networks among distinct POFD histological categories. METHODS: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on maxillary lesion tissues from three age- and sex-matched POFD patients classified as Type I (n=1), Type II (n=1), and Type III (n=1). After stringent quality control, 24,567 cells (median 1,762 genes/cell) were integrated and clustered. Ligand-receptor interactions were inferred using CellChat. RESULTS: + + + + + LTB TXNIP FTH1 PABPC1 S100A8/9 CXCL8 CCL2/3/4 IL1B Four major lineages were resolved: mesenchyme, lymphoid, myeloid, endovascular. Lymphoid representation differed across subtypes (Type I 1.00%, Type II 5.10%, Type III 10.90%), whereas endovascular fractions showed an inverse pattern (Type I 25.10%, Type II 9.90%, Type III 4.50%). Sub-clustering identified five lymphoid and six myeloid subsets. CD4T cells were most abundant in Type I (51.10%) but less represented in Type II (36.50%) and Type III (29.30%). CD8T cells constituted 2.10%, 11.90%, and 11.20% across Types I-III, respectively; germinal-center (GC) B cells were undetectable in Type I, minor in Type II (~1.60%), and prominent in Type III (~29.20%). Among myeloid cells, M1 macrophages comprised 9.90% in Type I, 25.70% in Type II, and 15.30% in Type III; osteoclasts were abundant in Type I (35.40%) but scarce in Types II and III (<5%). Dendritic cells (DCs) were absent in Type I yet detectable in Type II (1.90%) and Type III (2.60%). Network-central genes included,,, andfor CD4and GC B cells, and,,, andfor M1 macrophages and monocytes. Inter-cellular communication networks differed markedly by subtype: Type I and II displayed relatively simple interactomes, whereas Type III exhibited densely interconnected signaling with strengthened M2 macrophage-monocyte, M2 macrophage-GC B cell (CXCL12-CXCR4, APP-CD74), and GC B cell-monocyte axes, alongside attenuated CD4T cell-GC B cell (CLEC2D-KLRB1, ADGRE5-CD55) and M1 macrophage-CD4T cell crosstalk. Pathway enrichment revealed subtype-specific activation of oxidative phosphorylation, NF-κB, and antigen-presentation cascades across lymphoid and myeloid compartments. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first single-cell immune atlas of POFD, delineating lymphoid and myeloid heterogeneity across three histological subtypes. The identified subtype-specific markers and inter-cellular communication architectures offer candidate biomarkers for diagnostic stratification and reveal potential immunomodulatory targets for this disfiguring bone disorder.

title: Analysis of real-world multicenter experience with the large-bore CLEANER-Vac Thrombectomy System: An analysis of 200 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, represents a significant clinical entity associated with elevated morbidity and mortality rates. Conventional therapeutic approaches, such as systemic anticoagulation and thrombolytic agents, frequently yield suboptimal thrombus resolution. Mechanical thrombectomy has introduced a paradigm shift, enabling expeditious thrombus extraction while mitigating the chronic outcomes of suboptimally treated VTE and sequelae inherent to fibrinolytic therapies. The CLEANER Vac Thrombectomy System (Argon Medical Devices) is designed for controlled percutaneous venous thrombectomy. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world procedural efficacy, safety profile, and clinical utility of the CLEANER Vac system in a multicenter cohort comprising 200 patients presenting with symptomatic venous thrombus. METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter investigation included data from 200 patients who underwent intervention between October 2024 and January 2026 across 26 U.S. institutions. Eligible participants were adults aged ≥18 years with imaging-confirmed acute (<14 days) or subacute (14-28 days) VTE. Primary end points included thrombus clearance efficacy, segmented venous involvement, estimated blood loss, and intraprocedural adverse event incidence. RESULTS: The study cohort had a mean age of 64.5 (range, 25-90) years, with a gender distribution of 52% female (n = 104) and 48% male (n = 96). An average of 2.2 venous segments were treated per patient (range, 1-5). Mean preprocedure clot burden was 88.0%, which decreased to 10.5% postprocedure, culminating in a mean thrombus clearance of 88.0%. Overall, 76.0% of patients (n = 152) achieved ≥90% clot resolution. Adjunctive rotational maceration was used in 30% of cases, balloon venoplasty in 38%, and stent placement in 15%. Mean device utilization time was 8.0 minutes, with an average of 2.4 device passes per patient. Mean estimated blood loss was 320 (range, 50-750) mL. The overall complication rate was 2.4% (n = 5), consisting exclusively of minor access-site hematomas not attributed to the device. No serious adverse events were device-attributable within the 200-patient cohort. Procedures were predominantly classified as peripheral venous interventions (70%), with the remaining 30% encompassing alternative indications (eg, in-stent restenosis and transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt revisions). CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of 200 patients, the CLEANER Vac system demonstrated high procedural efficacy (88.0% mean clot clearance, 76% achieving ≥90% resolution) and a favorable overall safety profile. The findings support the potential role of this system in enabling rapid, single-session VTE treatment with constrained hemorrhagic liability and morbidity compared with catheter-directed thrombolysis. Prospective, longitudinal studies are warranted to evaluate long-term outcomes and delineate optimal patient stratification.

title: Outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair for uncomplicated subacute type B aortic dissection in the IRAD registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for uncomplicated type B acute aortic dissection (TBAAD) remains controversial. Compared with best medical therapy (BMT), TEVAR has demonstrated benefits for aortic remodeling; however, this intervention has procedure-related risks. METHODS: The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection database was queried from January 1996 to September 2023 for all uncomplicated TBAAD cases. Patients receiving TEVAR during the subacute phase (sTEVAR; 15-90 days) and BMT were included in this study. Baseline comorbidities were recorded. The primary outcome was survival at 4 years. The secondary outcomes included delayed aortic interventions, progression of aortic disease, new dissection, rehospitalization, rupture, and stroke. RESULTS: During the study period, 1373 patients with uncomplicated TBAAD were entered into the registry and had follow-up data available. In addition, 63 patients (4.6%) underwent sTEVAR, and 1310 (95.4%) received BMT. The 4-year survival rate was similar between the groups (sTEVAR 87% vs BMT 84%, P = .925). At 3 years, the sTEVAR group had higher rates of new dissection (13.9% vs 4.8%, P = .002), all within 1 year of TEVAR. Progression of dissection, aneurysmal degeneration, reintervention, rupture, stroke, and rehospitalization were comparable between the groups. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with BMT, sTEVAR led to similar survival rates. New dissection was higher in the sTEVAR group. TEVAR may have a role in uncomplicated subacute TBAAD, and further randomized trials are essential to identify which patients benefit from this intervention.

Compared with best medical therapy (BMT), TEVAR has demonstrated benefits for aortic remodeling; however, this intervention has procedure-related risks. METHODS: The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection database was queried from January 1996 to September 2023 for all uncomplicated TBAAD cases.

title: Intraportal Rupture of a Hepatic Hydatid Cyst Complicated by Arterioportal Fistula and Hepatic Artery Pseudoaneurysm.
abstract: A 71-year-old woman with known hepatic hydatid disease presented with fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, and jaundice. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with MR cholangiopancreatography revealed rupture of a right hepatic hydatid cyst with intraportal hydatid dissemination associated with a hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm and an arterioportal fistula. The patient rapidly developed severe acute cholangitis with multiorgan failure. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) allowed extraction of the hydatid material and biliary stenting, followed by selective endovascular embolization of the hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm. Despite combined endoscopic and interventional management, the patient progressed to refractory multiorgan failure and died. The present case illustrates a rare and life-threatening vascular complication of hepatic hydatid disease, emphasizing the importance of early imaging diagnosis and multidisciplinary management. In the present case, simultaneous portal and arterial involvement was associated with an unfavorable outcome.

title: The Effectiveness of Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Topical Application Versus Injection in the Healing of Chronic Venous Ulcers.
abstract: Introduction Chronic venous leg ulcers (VLUs) are common lower-limb wounds associated with delayed healing, recurrence, pain, impaired mobility, reduced quality of life, and increased healthcare costs. Although compression therapy remains the standard treatment, many ulcers heal slowly or remain resistant, highlighting the need for effective adjunctive therapies. Autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is rich in platelets and growth factors that promote angiogenesis, fibroblast proliferation, collagen synthesis, granulation tissue formation, and re-epithelialization, making it a promising regenerative therapy for chronic venous ulcers. However, existing evidence is limited due to small sample sizes, methodological heterogeneity, and variability in PRP preparation. Systematic reviews have therefore recommended well-designed prospective randomized trials to establish its efficacy and safety. Aims and objectives The study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of PRP topical application, PRP injection, and saline dressings in chronic VLUs, with the primary objective based on complete ulcer healing and percentage reduction in ulcer size, while assessing ulcer recurrence and early treatment-related complications constituted the secondary endpoints. Recurrence here is defined as re-appearance of the ulcer after its complete healing at the same site. Methodology This prospective randomized controlled trial was conducted over 18 months at JSS Medical College and Hospital, Mysuru, Karnataka, India. A total of 63 adults with chronic VLUs (>6 weeks) were randomly allocated into three groups: group A (topical PRP dressing), group B (local PRP injection), and group C (saline dressing). All patients received a standard four-layer compression therapy. Autologous PRP was prepared using a double-spin centrifugation technique and administered weekly for four weeks. Patients were followed for six months. Primary outcomes included complete ulcer healing and percentage reduction in ulcer area, while recurrence and treatment-related complications were assessed as secondary outcomes using SPSS Version 28 (p < 0.05). Results Baseline comparability was noted among groups for age, sex, BMI, HbA1c, platelet count, ankle-brachial pressure index, ulcer duration, and initial ulcer area. At six weeks, complete healing of the ulcer was much greater in group B (33.3%) than in group A (9.5%) and group C (0%) (p = 0.0064). At three months, the mean ulcer area was minimal in group B (1.30 ± 1.61 cm²) compared to group A (3.15 ± 3.01 cm²) and group C (6.19 ± 4.49 cm²) (p < 0.0001). The percentage reduction in ulcer area at three months was highest in group B (91.80 ± 8.05%), followed by group A (78.29 ± 17.68%) and group C (62.34 ± 19.06%). The mean healing duration was the shortest in group B (11.20 ± 2.18 weeks) (p = 0.0001). The rates of recurrence and complications were minimal and similar. Conclusion Autologous PRP is a safe and effective adjunct for chronic VLUs. Both PRP topical application and injection improved healing compared with saline dressing, while PRP injection achieved earlier healing, greater ulcer area reduction, and shorter healing time, making it the preferred PRP delivery method.

title: Perioperative Predictors and Temporal Trajectories of Postoperative Cognitive Decline After Carotid Endarterectomy: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Carotid artery stenosis is a well-established risk factor for vascular cognitive impairment. Although carotid endarterectomy (CEA) reduces the risk of ischemic stroke, its effect on cognitive function remains uncertain. Most previous studies have relied on mean changes in cognitive scores and have not defined postoperative cognitive decline using patient-level thresholds for the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Moreover, few studies have integrated perioperative variables across baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative domains to examine heterogeneity in cognitive outcomes. We therefore defined postoperative cognitive decline using threshold-based MoCA changes and prospectively evaluated perioperative factors associated with distinct cognitive outcomes after CEA. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled older patients undergoing elective CEA under general anesthesia. Of 183 patients screened, 162 were ultimately enrolled and analyzed. All patients were managed according to standardized anesthetic and surgical protocols. Preoperative clinical, laboratory, and imaging variables, intraoperative hemodynamic parameters, and postoperative clinical indicators were collected. The primary outcome was cognitive decline at discharge, defined as a decrease of ≥2 points from baseline in the MoCA score. The secondary outcome was cognitive decline at 30 days, defined as a ≥3-point decrease in the telephone MoCA (t-MoCA) score relative to the corresponding baseline domains. RESULTS: Among the 162 enrolled patients, preoperative triglyceride level, preoperative cerebral hypoperfusion volume, surgical laterality, intraoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) decline, and visual analogue scale (VAS) on postoperative day 1 were independently associated with early postoperative cognitive decline. A prediction model incorporating these five factors achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.752 (95% CI: 0.670-0.835) for cognitive decline before discharge. For 30-day cognitive decline, the model demonstrated an AUC of 0.717 (95% CI: 0.606-0.828). All patients with complete 30-day follow-up were stratified into four cognitive trajectory subtypes, and their longitudinal cognitive changes were visualized using a Sankey diagram. CONCLUSIONS: A perioperative model incorporating metabolic, cerebral perfusion, surgical, hemodynamic, and pain-related variables may help identify patients at increased risk of cognitive decline after CEA. The trajectory analysis further reveals heterogeneous postoperative cognitive patterns, including transient, delayed, and persistent decline. These findings support individualized perioperative risk assessment and structured cognitive follow-up. However, no internal or external validation was performed, and further testing is required in larger multicenter cohorts.

title: Incidence, timing, severity, and predictors of venous thromboembolism after open abdominal wall reconstruction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolic events, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, represent serious and potentially preventable complications following open abdominal wall reconstruction. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of venous thromboembolic events after open abdominal wall reconstruction. METHODS: A single-institution prospectively maintained database was queried for open abdominal wall reconstruction (2010-2025). Standard statistical analyses and multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of venous thromboembolic events. RESULTS: 2 2 Among 2,907 open abdominal wall reconstructions, 49 venous thromboembolic events (1.7%) occurred: 31 pulmonary embolisms ± deep vein thrombosis and 18 deep vein thromboses alone. Average body mass index was 34.6 ± 10.0 kg/m, and 18.4% had prior venous thromboembolic events. Preoperative chemoprophylaxis was administered in 77.6% of venous thromboembolic event cases, and 93.8% of patients who received postoperative chemoprophylaxis had no interruption. Compared with patients without venous thromboembolic events, those with venous thromboembolic events had larger defect sizes (314.5 ± 222.7 vs 199.8 ± 187.5 cm; P < .001) and longer operative times (233.4 ± 74.9 vs 187.2 ± 84.4 minutes; P < .001). Among 29 classified pulmonary embolisms, 13 were nonmassive, 12 submassive, and 4 massive/fatal. Advanced interventions were required in 12.2%, 16.3% required transfusion, and 16.3% underwent inferior vena cava filter placement. Among venous thromboembolic event patients, 40.8% required intensive care unit transfer, with 20.4% requiring reintubation. Average length of stay was longer in venous thromboembolic event patients (11.4 ± 9.8 vs 5.7 ± 8.8 days; P < .001). Multivariable regression identified body mass index (odds ratio, 1.09; 95% confidence interval, 1.04, 1.14; P < .001), prior venous thromboembolic events (odds ratio, 4.51; 95% confidence interval, 1.91, 10.62; P < .001), and operative time (odds ratio, 1.005; 95% confidence interval, 1.001, 1.010; P = .008) as independent predictors of venous thromboembolic event. CONCLUSION: Postoperative venous thromboembolic event following open abdominal wall reconstruction is uncommon but associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Higher body mass index, prior venous thromboembolic event, and longer operative time independently predicted venous thromboembolic event, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and prevention strategies.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolic events, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, represent serious and potentially preventable complications following open abdominal wall reconstruction. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of venous thromboembolic events after open abdominal wall reconstruction. METHODS: A single-institution prospectively maintained database was queried for open abdominal wall reconstruction (2010-2025).

title: Balloon Landmark-Assisted Re-entry Using a Re-entry Catheter for Femoropopliteal Chronic Total Occlusion: A Case Report.
abstract: Re-entry catheters are effective devices for achieving true lumen re-entry during endovascular therapy (EVT) for femoropopliteal chronic total occlusion (FP-CTO). However, accurate orientation of the catheter may be difficult when angiographic visualization of the target lumen is inadequate. We report a case of successful revascularization using an inflated balloon as a fluoroscopic landmark to facilitate re-entry catheter orientation. An 81-year-old man presented with symptomatic left lower extremity ischemia caused by FP-CTO. Two previous EVT procedures had failed because guidewire re-entry into the true lumen could not be achieved after subintimal passage. During the third EVT, the retrograde guidewire remained within the true lumen, whereas the antegrade guidewire advanced within the subintimal space. Because angiographic localization of the re-entry point was difficult, a 5 mm balloon was inflated within the subintimal space and used as a fluoroscopic landmark to determine the orientation of the re-entry catheter. After balloon deflation, the re-entry cannula was advanced from the true lumen toward the subintimal space, enabling successful guidewire passage and subsequent stent implantation. The procedure was completed using only 25 mL of contrast medium. The patient's symptoms resolved, and the ankle-brachial index improved from 0.64 to 1.08. This case suggests that an inflated balloon may serve as a useful fluoroscopic landmark for re-entry catheter orientation when conventional angiographic localization is difficult. In this case, the technique facilitated re-entry catheter orientation and successful guidewire crossing despite limited angiographic visualization. Its potential contribution to contrast minimization, particularly in patients with impaired renal function, requires further evaluation.

However, accurate orientation of the catheter may be difficult when angiographic visualization of the target lumen is inadequate. We report a case of successful revascularization using an inflated balloon as a fluoroscopic landmark to facilitate re-entry catheter orientation.

title: Recurrent venous thromboembolism despite natural cycle frozen embryo transfer in a woman with a history of pregnancy-related venous thromboembolism: A case report.
abstract: in vitro Pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. Pregnancies achieved byfertilization carry an increased risk of VTE, particularly during early gestation. A 33-year-old woman developed deep vein thrombosis during late pregnancy in her first spontaneous conception despite no identifiable thrombophilia. During a subsequent pregnancy achieved by natural cycle frozen embryo transfer, which was selected to avoid exogenous estrogen exposure and potentially reduce the thrombotic risk compared with hormone replacement cycles, she developed recurrent VTE at 8 weeks of gestation. Anticoagulation therapy was initiated, and an inferior vena cava (IVC) filter was placed in late pregnancy because of persistent thrombus and delivery-related risk. A cesarean section was successfully performed, and the IVC filter was removed postpartum after regression of the thrombus. Although natural cycle frozen embryo transfer may reduce the thrombotic risk compared with hormone replacement cycles, it does not eliminate the risk of recurrent VTE in women with a history of pregnancy-associated thrombosis. Early initiation of anticoagulation and careful peripartum management, including selective use of IVC filters, are essential in high-risk patients.

title: Clinical Profile and Visual Outcomes of Pre- and Postembolization of Carotid-cavernous Fistula-induced Glaucoma.
abstract: Carotid-cavernous fistula (CCF) requires comprehensive postembolization management to address secondary complications, including glaucoma. A 70-year-old male presented with the inability to open his left eye, progressive eyelid swelling, and orbital congestion. Examination revealed severe conjunctival chemosis with dilated episcleral vessels, elevated intraocular pressure (IOP; 20 mmHg), and corneal Descemet's folds. Imaging confirmed an arteriovenous fistula at the left sphenoid bone draining into the superior ophthalmic vein. The patient underwent successful endovascular embolization of the left sphenoid arteriovenous fistula. Medical management included topical dorzolamide, beta-blockers, and oral acetazolamide for IOP control. Postembolization, there was a significant reduction in orbital congestion, improved eyelid function, and stabilization of IOP. Visual acuity improved from counting fingers to 6/12 with successful preservation of optic nerve function. This case highlights the importance of timely multispecialty collaboration between ophthalmology and interventional radiology in managing CCF-related secondary glaucoma.

title: Feasibility and Clinical Outcomes of a 6-Month Home-Based Telerehabilitation Program in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Prospective Single-Arm Study.
abstract: p p p p (1) Background: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity and functional impairment. This study evaluated the feasibility and adherence of a 6-month home-based telerehabilitation (TR) program and longitudinal changes in functional capacity, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and selected cardiometabolic parameters. (2) Methods: This prospective, single-arm study enrolled 42 patients with PAD. Daily ambulation was monitored using a Xiaomi Smart Band 8, and participants received weekly telephone counseling. Assessments were performed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. (3) Results: Median daily step count increased from 5868 to 6905 steps/day (< 0.001), whereas attainment of progressively increasing weekly targets decreased from 58.33% to 16.66% (< 0.001). Median 6 min walk test (6MWT) distance increased from 390 m to 445 m at 6 months, a 55 m increase (= 0.001). HRQoL, systolic blood pressure, body mass index, and total cholesterol showed significant longitudinal changes, while resting ankle-brachial index and selected cardiopulmonary exercise testing parameters remained relatively stable (> 0.05). (4) Conclusions: The TR program was feasible and accompanied by increased activity and improved walking capacity. The divergence between absolute activity and target attainment supports multidimensional adherence assessment. Causal effects cannot be established given the single-arm design.

title: Endovascular Recanalization of Non-Acute Vertebrobasilar Occlusion in Progressive Posterior Circulation Ischemia: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Unlike acute basilar artery occlusion, non-acute vertebrobasilar occlusion has limited evidence for intervention and requires individualized risk assessment. CASE PRESENTATION: A 62-year-old woman developed progressive vertigo, diplopia, dysarthria, and gait ataxia over ten days. Dual antiplatelet therapy was started after posterior circulation ischemia was suspected, but symptoms continued to progress. MRI showed acute to subacute left cerebellar infarction, and CTA showed absent antegrade basilar opacification with collateral distal filling. DSA showed distal left vertebral artery occlusion, retrograde basilar filling through posterior communicating artery collaterals, and hypoplastic right vertebral artery. Endovascular recanalization was performed after multidisciplinary review and informed consent. Intraluminal crossing, stepwise angioplasty, and stent reconstruction restored antegrade basilar flow without angiographic complications. NIHSS improved from 5 to 2 at discharge, and mRS was 1 at 30 days. No follow-up vascular imaging was available. CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates technical feasibility in selected non-acute vertebrobasilar occlusion, but does not establish medical treatment failure, causal recovery, generalizable safety, or long-term durability.
